sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, lettera, other, relazione
sources.legate: Abbate Gio. Andrea Ricci (Abbas Joannes Andreas Riccius, Politianus, canon of St Peter's), delegate of the Vatican Chapter
sources.deputy: Abbate Gio. Andrea Ricci (Abbas Joannes Andreas Riccius, Politianus, canon of St Peter's), delegate of the Vatican Chapter
sources.rubric_latin: Relazione del seguito nella Venuta dell'Illmo e Rmo Sig.r Can.co Gio. Andrea Ricci in Montepulciano per coronare la Bma Vergine detta di S. Martino esistente nella Chiesa Cattedrale
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'duas coronas aureas valoris et aestimationis scut. centum monetae Romanae'. f.188r: letter of Gio. Andrea Ricci from Montepulciano, 31 Oct 1707, announcing his arrival and reception by the Bishop, Chapter, Magistrato and the Operai della Madonna di S. Martino. f.189r: silversmith's account ('Adi 30 Sett. 1700' - probably 1707) for two gold crowns, large and small, 153.85 scudi, 'Servirono p le Sacre Immagini della Sma Vergine e Suo Bambino Gesu nella Città di Monte Pulciano'; sums repeated on f.188v; wrapper f.194v 'Conto 2 ... Gio: Giardini Oref.'. ff.190r-192r, 196r-197v and 198r-v: three copies of the 'Relatione del seguito nella venuta ... Can.co Gio. Andrea Ricci in Montepulciano per coronare la Bma Vergine detta di S. Martino esistente nella Chiesa Cattedrale' (arrival dates garbled by OCR: '16 Ott.e 1701', '26 7bre 1760' with margin 'd'an: 1760', '5 Ott.e 1707'; the coronation day 6 November is consistent in all copies and the title leaf f.193v gives 1707). Coronation at the Mass after Communion; an instrument of consignment of the two crowns was rogated by the chancellor of the episcopal curia (not present; f.193v margin '(non vi è l'origine)'). f.195v margin: 'lettera delle M. S. ... Andrea Ricci ...'. The third copy of the relazione breaks off at f.198v, the last page of the range. | Two copies of the relazione (ff. 196r–198v), 'Memorie dello Scoprimento e Culto' drawn from episcopal visitations of 1610/1612 (ff. 200r–200v, two copies; ends 'De Anno 1707 ... ipsa Sacra Imago una cum Imagine Infantis Jesu in ejus sinu sedentis corona aurea fuit solemni pompa coronata'), Ricci's covering letter of the day after the crowning (f. 201r, OCR date 'Montepulciano 7 9.bre 1701' / 'Montegranaro 9 8br 1701', i.e. 7 Nov 1707), a 'Decretum 30 Junii 1704' of which only the heading was transcribed (f. 201v) — taken here as the concession date, medium certainty — and two copies of the notarial instrument of consignment (ff. 202r–203v; notary Oliverius Antonius Vannutius, chancellor Vincentius Pallini/Lattini; authenticated by the vicar general 15/18 Nov 1707; margin: 'Instrum. Donationis ... Politiana die 5. [or 8.] 9bris 1707'). Coronation date: relazione says Ricci arrived 26 Sept (OCR '1760') / 5 Oct 1707 and the ceremony was 'il dì 6. Nov.'; letter 'Coronatione di ieri mattina' confirms 6 Nov 1707; the instrument's OCR 'die sexta Mens. Sept./Feb.' is presumably 'Novembris'. f. 204v margin: 'Altra lettera del d.º S.r Ab.e Ricci ... relat.e ... alla coronaz.ne' (text not transcribed). Isolated margin words 'Antonelli' (f. 199r) and 'loco detto Sevratto' (f. 204v) unexplained — the latter probably belongs to the following Tersatto dossier. f. 196r opens with the head of the relazione; whether earlier Montepulciano documents precede f. 196r cannot be seen from this range. The instrument also alludes to the Chapter having earlier crowned images 'in celeberrimo D. Blasii Templo' (S. Biagio, Montepulciano) — not documented in this range.

sources.rubric_latin: Instrumentum Donationis Duarum Coronæ aureæ, factæ Imagini B. M. V. miraculosæ ... in Sacro, et Reali Monasterio Montis Virginis maioris de Alvito, factæ in Actis Regiis Die 17. Maij 1712
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Three heavily garbled OCR passes of one Latin attestation by the archbishop of Benevento ('Athanasius Ursinus, S. Beneventanae Ecclesiae Archiepiscopus'; signature OCR 'J. d. B. Card. Spinus Archiepiscopus' — i.e. Cardinal Orsini, archbishop of Benevento 1686–1724, inferred), dated Benevento 9 Jan 1708, testifying to the antiquity and miracles of an image of the Virgin painted by St Luke: brought by Baldwin, Emperor of Constantinople; 'Catharina Balduini'; Frederick's army 'anno 1239 juxta Beneventanam'; 'Brundusium'; 'Civitate Abellina' (Avellino); 'Monte praefato adscendere'; 'Guilelmo Abbati'; 'Congregationis Montis Virginis' — legend elements pointing to the Madonna di Montevergine, but one pass places the image 'in Ecclesia S. Angeli ...' (S. Angelo a Cupolo?) and another 'Monialium Asceterii', so the church is not securely read. Margin 'Car. ly / januarij Co:nat.' (Coronat.?) and '2/3'. Attestation only: no decree, crowns, deputy or coronation date in this range; dossier presumably continues past f. 215r. Wrapper f. 214v 'Corone d'oro' (margin '514') may belong to this dossier. | Dossier contents: (a) attestations on the origin of the image by the Archbishop of Benevento (OCR 'Athanasius Ursinus' / 'Card. Spinus Archiepiscopus', i.e. Card. Orsini), dated 9 January 1708, margin 'Attestati circa l'origine della Madonna di Monte Vergine nella Diocesi di Benevento, o sia Provincia del 1708' and 'Monte Vergine a del 1708' (heavily garbled Latin, ff. 215r–218v); (b) conto of the silversmith Gio. Giardini for two crowns 'per mandare alla Chiesa detta di Monte uergine di Napoli', settled 23 May 1711, 295 scudi (ff. 216r–217v); (c) decree 12 July 1711 (Lib. Decr. XX f. 8v) suspending the coronation because the image already had a gold crown, remitting the question to the Nuncio (f. 219r); (d) notarial copy of the donation instrument by D. Thomas Cervanetta of Mercogliano, dated in the text 'Die Decimoquarto mensis Maij' 1712 (margin says 17 May 1712), incorporating the Chapter's commission letter of Rome 24 [April] 1712, the 'Ordo servandi in Tradendis Coronis Aureis', and the brief of Clement XI of 29 April 1712 granting a plenary indulgence (ff. 220r–223v); (e) relazione of Canon Howard's journey (25 April–21 May 1712), coronation performed after first Vespers of Pentecost, i.e. Saturday 14 May 1712 (heading 'alli 14. di Maggio 1712'), ff. 224r–229v, with a printed 'avviso' from Naples quoted; (f) letter of the Abbot General D. Vito Antonio Pastorale, Montevergine 15 May 1712, and minuta of the Chapter's reply 5 June (or Aug.) 1712 (ff. 230v–233v). No explicit concession date appears; the Chapter's letter says only 'havendo Noi già da molto tempo Decretata la Corona d'oro'. Margin at f. 223v reads 'Montis Virginis maioris de Alvito' (OCR; expected 'de Monte'). 'cap. 63. pag: 435.' (f. 229r) and 'Lib. III. de S. M. V. a pag. 25' (f. 230r) may be bibliographic rather than register references.

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 290r–301r
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, instrumentum donationis, lettera, other, supplica
sources.legate: Prospero Lambertini, canon of St Peter's, Archbishop of Theodosia (delegate), who by letter of 21 July 1724 subdelegated Francesco Maria Carafa, Bishop of Nola; the crowns were imposed by Card. (Francesco) Pignatelli, Archbishop of Naples
sources.deputy: Prospero Lambertini, canon of St Peter's, Archbishop of Theodosia (delegate), who by letter of 21 July 1724 subdelegated Francesco Maria Carafa, Bishop of Nola; the crowns were imposed by Card. (Francesco) Pignatelli, Archbishop of Naples
sources.rubric_latin: Memoriale dato da d. PP. Teatini di S. Paolo Magg.re di Napoli, che supplicano il R.mo Cap.lo p la Coronat.ne della Mad.na della Purità, che si venera nella loro Chiesa con una Let.ta del S.r Card. Pignatelli
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'ad formam semicirculi constructas et perforatas, unciarum novem, valoris ducatorum circiter ducentum'; Giardini's account 174:97 scudi. Petitioner: Clerici Regolari Teatini di S. Paolo Maggiore, Napoli (Provost D. Filippo Sifola, Vicar D. Casimiro Salmieri, and the fathers), supported by a letter of Card. Pignatelli. Supplica dated 'Napoli 4 di 9bre 1713' (= 4 Nov 1713); letter of Card. Pignatelli, Napoli 3 March 1714; letter of P. Savino, canon of St Peter's (undated); margin note reads 'Concesso 27 Marze 1700' — the year is OCR-suspect and 1714 is inferred from the surrounding dates, so concession_date is an inference. 'Other' = extract from Carlo Celano's Notizie di Napoli (1725) on S. Paolo Maggiore, the church of Suor Orsola Benincasa and S. Chiara (Giotto Madonna) — the latter two images are merely described, not crowned; also payment mandates to the silversmith Giacomo Antonio Giardini (30 scudi on 14 Jan 1717) and Giardini's account for the two crowns (174:97 scudi), which mislabels the church as 'S. Carlo de Padri Teatini'. Instrument (Latin, Naples, 7 Sept 1724, notary Thomas Cerillo, copy authenticated 1 Feb 1725) inserts Lambertini's letter of Roma 21 July 1724 ('corrente anno 1624' is OCR for 1724). Margin at f.300v labels it 'Instrumentum Coronationis Sae: Imaginis B. M. V. Laetitiae in Ecclesia Divi Pauli Maj. ... Neapoli factae die 7. Septembris 1724' ('Laetitiae' is probably an OCR/archivist slip for Puritatis). A further stray margin note at f.301r, 'Instrumentum Coronationis Sac: Imagini B.M.V. Luscintani', is unreadable and not tied to any document in the range.

sources.rubric_latin: dat, donat, et concedit Be- atissimæ Virgini nuncupat. S.ti Brijj huius Ill.mo Civitatis Urbevetanae ... Duas Coronas Aureas ... in antiquiss. et Insigni Ecclesia Cathedrali
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'Duas Coronas Aureas', weight 7½ oz and 2 denari of gold, 276 scudi 8 [baiocchi?] Roman money excluding the goldsmith's fee. Petitioner: City of Orvieto (Confaloniere e Conservatori / publico Consiglio) through Bishop Vincenzo de' Conti degli Atti; crowns received in the instrument by Giovanni Battista Gualterio, camerlengo of the Fabbrica of the Cathedral. Only the first two pages of the Latin donation instrument fall within this range (f.142r–v); it breaks off at 'coronata' and continues past the range. Coronation date is the date of the instrument (8 June 1704, Clement XI anno IV), which states the crowns were brought 'ad effectum coronandi' and that the images were 'postea coram eisdem ... coronata' — read as same-day crowning, not explicitly confirmed. Diocese inferred from 'Civitatis Urbevetanae' and the mention of its bishop. The deputy's surname is OCR-garbled ('Cia- Siy Coccianus'); the bishop is named only as 'R.mo D. Fabritio Ep.'. No concession decree or margin note is visible in this range. The image is apparently the Madonna venerated in the Cappella di S. Brizio of Orvieto Cathedral (the text says 'nuncupat. S.ti Brijj'); the Child is named ('illiusque D.ni Filij'). The margin note on f.122r mentioning an 'Ab.te d'Orvieto: Andrea Ricci' may relate to this dossier. | Instrument of donation dated 8 June 1704 (notary Carlo Fontana of Orvieto), witnesses Leone Albergio and Monaldo Aurelio; the printed Racconto (by canon Lattanzio Silvestrucci, Orvieto: Livio Tosini) confirms the crowning on 8 June 1704 during solemn Mass, with feasts 8-10 June; a sonnet to D. Annibale Albani at f.159v. Margin note at f.143v reads 'conceditur 16 Jul. 1896' — year clearly garbled by OCR (1696 or 1703 possible), so concession_date left null; the same note reads 'Instrum. donationis duarum Coronarum aurearum factae Imaginis miraculosae B. M. V. in Ecclesia ... Civitatis Urbevet. ... die 27. May 1704' (partly garbled). The image was formerly called 'Santa Maria prisca' and 'S. Maria della Stella'. The bishop's name is garbled as 'Fabritio Ep.' in the Latin instrument but given as Vincenzo de' Conti degli Atti in the Racconto.

sources.rubric_latin: Instrum. Donationis Duar.m Coronar.m aurear.m fact simulacro miraculoso SS.mæ ... in Ecclesia Metropolitana Hydrunti Die 7 Maij 1705
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), value 78 1/2 scudi d'oro in oro. Petitioner: Clero e Città d'Otranto; concession originally granted at the prayers of Card. de Aste (then a member of the Chapter). Concession date taken from the endorsement on f.82r ('Instrum Donationis duar Coronar aurear / concessio 14 Maii 1691', with silversmith Gio. Giardini's signature on f.82v); its attribution to Otranto is inferred (medium) from the 1705 letter stating the crown had been 'destinata' earlier at Card. de Aste's request and from the archbishop's information letter of 6/20 June 1691 (two copies, ff.83r-84r, endorsed 'Lettera di Mons. Arcivescovo d'Otranto in ordine alla Corona d'oro'). Instrument (two copies, ff.87r-88r) is dated 'Die vero Septima Martij' 1705, notary Angelo Stephanoch of Otranto; the archivist's endorsement reads '7 Maij 1705' but the archbishop's covering letter of 22 March 1705 (f.89r) confirms March. Conto on f.85r (Dom.co Vannini) for two crowns, 154:50 in all, sits inside this dossier and is presumed to belong to it. The 1691 letter records the statue's return from Valona (Vlorë) after the Turkish sack of 1480 and a jubilee granted by Pius V in 1564. Loose margin words 'Oronzo', '14', '85' on ff.85v-86v.
Reported by Balzamo 2023, not read at first hand. Year only; one of only two coronations in Venetian territory (the other Verona 1709).

sources.rubric_latin: RELAZIONE DELLA MIRACOLOSA STATUA DELLA SS. MA VERGINE DI LIBERA INFERNO Che si adora nella Chiesa Metropolitana di Palermo
sources.notes: Crowns: one mentioned ('la Corona d'Oro ... p. una di d.te Imagini'; 'una di quelle Corone d'oro'); number not otherwise specified. f.178v: label 'Decretum 23 Febr. 1699' (margin '351') - placed here on position only; it may instead belong to the preceding leaf (Genoa/S. Maria Liberatrice certificate of 1742), so no concession_date is asserted. f.179r: order of 5 Dec 1728 by M. Maffei, Dean of the Chapter, to the computista Clemente Polidori to pay 71 scudi from the Sforza deposit at the Banco di S. Spirito to the silversmith Bartolomeo Borioni on account of the gold crown he is making for the image in the Metropolitan of Palermo 'Sancti- Marie libera Inferni'. f.180r-185v: printed booklet 'Relazione della miracolosa statua della SS.ma Vergine di Libera Inferno che si adora nella Chiesa Metropolitana di Palermo, cavata dal libro Palermo divoto di Maria del fu Canonico D. Antonino Mongitore', Palermo, Angelo Felicella, 1750, reprinted by the Chapter of the Metropolitan on the occasion of the coronation with the Vatican Chapter's Sforza crown; it promises a later printed account of the ceremony (not in range). The ceremony date is not given. Margin numbers 179-183 are the booklet's pagination; f.185v margin '31-90 33-70 40 65' are sums.

sources.rubric_latin: Relazione intorno all'Imagine della B. V. delle Grazie che si venera nella Chiesa Catted.le di S. Cristoforo della Città della Penna Residenza de' Vescovi di Montefeltro
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), 65 scudi 1 denaro 21 grani of gold. Relazione (f. 104r-105v): image painted on the wall with the Child, altar consecrated 1215, lacrimation 20 March 1489, confraternity c. 1490 aggregated to the Gonfalone; 'coronata l'anno 1708 adì 15 Agosto' by Bishop Martorelli. Conto (f. 106r) dated 17 May 1705 for the two crowns, total 143:8 1/2, signed 'Tom.o Lannini Can.o Deput.o'; margin heading 'Relaz.e della B. V. nella Città di Penna, e Rieti' (Rieti unexplained). Latin instrument (f. 107r-107v) cites the Chapter's faculty 'Sub dat. Romæ 7 9mbris 1704' while the Chapter's Italian letter (f. 108r) is dated 'Roma 4. 9mbre 1707' (addressed 'Monsignor Corelli Vescovo di M.feltro', OCR for Martorelli) - year uncertain. The instrument's church reading 'Eccl.ia S.ti Arch.li Mich.is' conflicts with S. Christophori elsewhere and is probably OCR. Margin label f. 110v gives 'die 15. Aug.ti 1709' and the bishop's attestation 'Die 21 Augusti 1705' - both likely OCR/slips for 1708. The confraternity (Società della B. V. delle Grazie; deputies Gio. Carboni, Polidoro Valentini, Giuseppe Fabri) received the crowns and undertook the obligation. The cover f. 111v ('Decernitur Visitatio 10 Maii 1694 conceditur 11 Oct 1694') immediately follows this dossier but appears to belong to the unidentified 'Conto 2' at f. 112r; it may nevertheless be this image's concession.

sources.rubric_latin: Desiderano i R. P. D. di cotesta Chiesa di S. Fiorenzo, che dal nostro Capitolo si adorni con la Corona d'oro la S. Imagine della SS.ma Vergine esistente nella loro Chiesa
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Petitioner: the Fathers (Religiosi) of the church of S. Fiorenzo, Perugia ('R. P. D. di cotesta Chiesa di S. Fiorenzo'); margin f.176r 'Servit...' suggests Servites. Letter of the Chapter (Rome, 31 July 1697, signed Aurelio Vittorio canon secretary) to a bishop ('Mons. Patritio Vescovo di ...', address on verso 'Colligio Sapienza / Perugia') asking for information on the antiquity, fame of miracles and prior crowning of the image before deciding. Locality Perugia inferred from the address on f.170v. No concession in this range; the dossier ends at the last page of the range so may continue past it. | f.170r-v: letter of the Vatican Chapter, Rome 31 July 1697, to the Bishop of Perugia asking for information on antiquity, miracles and whether the image was already crowned. f.171r-171v and f.172r-v: two historical accounts (miracle of the mason's apprentice Camillo Serafini who tried to cover the image with lime, 1617; episcopal process 'Madonne S. Florentij'; translation into the church 1646); the second ends 'Fu coronata questa l'anno 1720 ... Monsig. Ansildi ... Vescovo di Perugia ... il di 4 Novembre'. f.173r: silversmith's account dated 5 Ottobre 1726 for two gold crowns for the images in S. Fiorenzo, Perugia (265:30 scudi, mandate 162 scudi signed Gio. A. Ricci Segr.); f.174v wrapper 'Conto delle Corone d'Oro con Giacomo Ant. Giardini Argent.'. The OCR year '1720' conflicts with the 1726 account; 1726-11-04 adopted as the coronation date (crowns made Oct 1726), so the date is inferred - medium confidence. f.176v margin notes: 'Madonna indos[?]', 'Diocesi di Perugia', 'Dalla Cancellaria Vescovile', 'possa N. 93', 'Armario N. 63', 'Peruggia'. No concession decree or date seen in range.

ex libr. XVIII. Decr. Cap. p. 6
sources.rubric_latin: Decreta fuit 17. Xbris 1696 corona redimita in die Assumptionis 1697 ex decr. caplanibus To. XVIII p. 13.
sources.notes: Crowns: one new gold crown for the Child ('una Corona d'oro lavorata con fiori e cartelle per il Bambino'); the existing crowns of the Virgin and Child recoloured and burnished. Petitioner: Capitolo e Canonici della Basilica di S. Pietro (the Chapter itself). Contents: decree 2 March 1697 deputing the Sacrista Maggiore and Fabretti to oversee restoration of the sacristy chapel where the image stands (100 scudi from the Fabbrica); account of 25 June 1697 for the Child's crown (39.45 scudi, signed Tomaso Vannini camerlengo), docket 'Gio: Giardini Orefice'; supplica to the Pope for a plenary indulgence for the crowning 'alli 14 del corrente mese d'Agosto', granted 7 Aug 1697 by Card. Albani 'pro unica vice'; a note (f.168r, dated 3 Jan 1695 by 'Parruccini Vic.o') that Innocent XII conceded the indulgence for the crowning after the Vespers of the Assumption, with f.168v recording an indulgence brief of 11 Aug 1695 (Caps. 1 fasc. 2), suggesting the crowning was first planned for 1695 and carried out in 1697; f.169r gives the inscription on the Child's crown 'Cap.lum S. Petri de urbe hanc cor. au. ex legato Ill.mi Com. Alex. Sfortiae An. 1697'. Coronation date: docket says 'in die Assumptionis 1697', supplica says 14 August (eve/after Vespers) — 15 Aug 1697 adopted, 14 Aug possible. f.167r is a later letter to Mons. Guerrieri asking that the image, 'la prima ad esser decorata della corona d'oro' in Sforza's lifetime, be crowned anew. OCR gives 'Madonna della Pieve' at f.168r for 'della Febre'. | f.168r (OCR) calls the image 'Madonna s:ma della Pieve ... nella Sagrestia della Basilica di S. Pietro' - almost certainly 'della Febre' as f.169r reads. f.168r: letter of the Vicar (Parruccini Vic.o) on the plenary indulgence granted by Innocent XII for the day of the coronation, 'Dati li 3. Gen. 1695'; f.168v: note on the Brief 'Dat. 11. Aug. 1695 = Caps. 1. fasc. 2.' and 'Decreta fuit 17. Xbris 1696 corona redimita in die Assumptionis 1697 ex decr. caplanibus To. XVIII p. 13'; f.169r: text of the inscription on the crown ('Cap.lum S. Petri de urbe hanc cor. au. ex legato Ill.mi Com. Alex. Sfortiae An. 1697'). Years 1695 vs 1696/97 may be OCR noise. This is the first leaf of the range; earlier documents of this dossier may lie in the preceding batch (not visible).

sources.rubric_latin: RELAZIONE DEL PRINCIPIO, E CAUSE DELLA VENERAZIONE DELL'IMMAGINE DELLA SANTISSIMA VERGINE DETTA DELLE GRAZIE DELLA TERRA DI S. GIOVANNI Da Coronarsi solennemente il dì 8. di Settembre 1704
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), weight 59 scudi d'oro meno 9 grani per conto. Petitioner: Operai of the Oratory (Giovanni Michele Santini, Alessandro de' Bessi, Vittorio de' Rossi, Antonio Camillo de' Giovini, Andrea del Bello) / Deputati sopra la Solennità. Instrument (two copies, ff.91r-92r) actum 8 Sept 1704 at S. Giovanni under Cosimo III, notary Ottaviano de' Pasquini(?) da Lastra/Camerina; crowning performed in the Oratory at pontifical Mass of Orazio 'de Lanciarichis' (Panciatichi), Bishop of Fiesole. Concession date from endorsement f.92v.01 'Romæ sub die 15 maii 1704' (reading as the decree date is an inference, medium). Second endorsement f.92v.02 is badly garbled ('B. M. V. de Rupe, sive nuncupatæ Tra:tarn ... Actum die 27 Aug. 1707') — likely OCR damage on the same instrument, not a separate event. Register ref 'Caps. 39. fasc. 38g' probably = 'Caps. 39. fasc. 3'. Conto on f.90r names the image as 'esistente nella cità di Fiesole in Toschana' (i.e. diocese). f.93v: a mostly unread conto by 'Gio. Giustini/Giardini Argentiere' with margin 'conceditur die 6 Octobr' (no year) and '5 Octobr' on f.94r — placement suggests it belongs to this dossier but it could concern another image. Printed Relazione (Firenze, Michele Nestenus, 1704) ff.94r-97v narrates the 1479 miracle of Mona Tancia and the 1596 fire. | Tail end of a printed historical relazione (long-s typography) that begins in the previous batch; the page opens mid-text ('E Fabio Segni col seguente'). The image's title is not given in this range: it is described as the miraculous painted image of the Virgin and Child at the Porta di S. Lorenzo of the Terra of S. Giovanni in Tuscany / Valdarno ('Beatus Aegidius in Valle Arnensi in Tuscia'; Florentine dominion), with the 1479 Mona Tancia milk miracle, the 1596 fire, privileges of Sixtus IV and Innocent VIII. The relazione closes 'si porta da Noi Deputati sopra la mentovata Incoronazione', so a coronation had been performed, but no date, deputy or concession appears here. The modern designation (Madonna delle Grazie, San Giovanni Valdarno) is an inference, not in the text. Country inferred from Tuscany/Firenze.

sources.notes: Pius VII crowned the image in person: 'post annum, promissa exsecutus, istic miserentissimae Matris imaginem pretiosa corona redimiit'. The year 1815 is derived from the rubric ('centum annis ante') read against the centenary solemnities announced for 7-13 May 1915 - not printed as a numeral, so treat the year as reconstructed. sources.notes: Attests the personal coronation by Pius VII: 'eundemque anno post, aurea corona simulacro Savonensi imposita, votum Mariae Auxiliatrici christianorum solvisse' ('abhinc fere centum annis'). Ferrari, Archbishop of Milan, as his Legate to the centenary solemnities - not to a coronation - so the legate field is left null. The letter begins on printed p. 201; the passage's printed_page is 202.

sources.notes: Letter for the fourth centenary of the 1536 apparition to Antonio Botta. Quod quidem contigit, quum Pius VII ... die x Maii anno MDCCCXV ...' and later 'dies x Maii, quo Virginis simulacro aurea corona per augustas manus imposita est'. Passage printed_page is 267, but the act plainly begins on p. 266 (verified against the volume text); page 266 used. Rubric OCR 'NOSTRA®' repaired to 'NOSTRAE'.

sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child), weight 'centum sexaginta'. Cover f. 113v: 'Visitatio Decernitur 11 Julii 1695', 'Decreverunt 29 Julii 1695' ('Gio: Gianlorenzi Ajo' unexplained). Ricci's letter to the Chapter, Siena 8 June 1704 (f. 118r) and relazione (f. 119r-120v): crowning on Saturday 7 June 1704 after Vespers. Discrepancies: heading f. 115v says 'coronata li 5 Giugno 1707' and the relazione once says 'Sabbato 2 Giugno' - both OCR/slips; 7 June 1704 is consistent throughout. The margin at f. 122r ('... sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 24r–69v
sources.act_type: Chapter dossier: conto argentiere, decretum, instrumentum donationis, other, relazione, stampa, supplica
sources.legate: Camillo Mugiasca (Mugiacea), canon of the Vatican Basilica, 'ad haec specialiter deputatus'
sources.deputy: Camillo Mugiasca (Mugiacea), canon of the Vatican Basilica, 'ad haec specialiter deputatus'
sources.rubric_latin: I Deputati della Madonna ss.ma di Tirano in Valtellina Dioc. di Como ... / margin f.26v: '10 Apr. 1690 Decreta fuit'
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'duas Coronas Auri', 18 ounces, value 200 scudi auri de Camera (instrument); 'doi Corone di Oro ... de la Madonna e del suo Bambino' (silversmith's account). Petitioner: Deputati della Madonna SS.ma di Tirano (Deputati et Rectores of the sanctuary: Antonio Meriti, Orazio Francesco Lucino, Domenico Mattio, Giacomo Liazzi), through a supplica to Pope Alexander VIII; the commemorative inscription says the honour was procured by Francesco Saverio Guicciardi, Bishop of Narni. Only the undated petition to the Pope (f.24r-v) and an inserted printed sheet with Latin captions listing the Virgin's miracles ('Præsentissima Virginis Tiranensis ope', 'Vbi steterunt pedes Mariæ', 'cum privil.') fall within this range; no decree, instrument or coronation date is visible here. The dossier runs to the end of the batch (f.25v blank) and is shared with the next batch, so any concession/coronation documents would lie past this range. Image subject not specified in these pages (whether with Child unknown). 'Levmaria' in the OCR is unclear (perhaps 'Lombardia'/'Germania'). | Whole range is one dossier. Contents: supplica of the Deputati to Alexander VIII (ff.24r-24v, docket f.26v with margin note '10 Apr. 1690 Decreta fuit' = concession date); printed devotional sheets inserted at f.25r ('Praesentissima Virginis Tiranensis ope', 'Ubi steterunt pedes Mariae') and ff.36r-37v ('Raptus Angelorum', 'Virgo Tiranensis'; one sheet marked 'Rinouato dal Bianchi 1780', a later insertion); silversmith's account f.27r (two gold crowns for Madonna and Bambino, total 239.20 scudi after tare; silversmith named in margin f.32v as 'Gio: Giardini Arg.o'; ff.31r-32v otherwise only page numerals); notarial instrument ff.28r-30r drawn by Paolo Francesco Bononi, notary of Como, dated Friday 29 Sept 1690 (weekday verified), crowns placed on the heads of the images of the Virgin and Child in the church, hymn Ave Maris Stella sung; vicar-general's attestation dated Como 7 Oct 1690; authenticated copy (f.33r) of the inscription on a large commemorative 'Quadro' hung in the sanctuary, signed by canon G. B. Robustelli; Mugiasca's relazione ff.34r-35r (left Como 1 Sept 1690, crowning on the feast of St Michael with ~20,000 people, Mass sung by the archpriest, Capuchin panegyric); f.35v is a stray unrelated fragment of Chapter business; ff.38r-48v a printed book 'Breve Istoria della miracolosissima Madonna di Tirano' by Gio. Antonio Cornacchi (1621; reprint Parma/Milano 1747), which runs on past f.48v. The place is called 'Tivano' in parts of the instrument (OCR/scribal variant of Tirano). The relazione (f.34v) has the panegyric 'in Lode della Beata Vergine del Lago' — likely OCR garbling, since every other document names Tirano. The instrument locates Tirano in the 'Statuum Ill.mor D.norum Rhetorum' (under the Grisons in 1690); country given as Italy on the basis of the place itself (the supplica calls it 'uno dei più famosi Santuarii d'Italia'). The crowned object is described as 'la Statua in mezzo la Chiesa' in the relazione, while the book describes the altar ancona with the effigy of Our Lady standing; the instrument speaks of two 'Sacrae Imagines' (Virgin and Child). No 'Lib.'/'Caps.' register cross-references occur in this range; the marginal numerals (30-46) are foliation/page counts only. Supplica begins with its heading at f.24r, so the dossier appears to start here, but folios before 24r were not visible. | Only a printed booklet (chapters IV to the end, with 'Addizioni', twelve Latin 'Elogia' on the Venerable Mario Omodei, and a closing protestation signed 'Homodaeus Anonymus') is in range; it begins mid-way (printed p. 45 at f. 46r), so chapters I-III and any supplica/decree/instrument for this image lie before pb 113. No coronation document, concession date or deputy is visible in the range. Diocese taken from the booklet itself ('Archivio del Vescovato di Como', 'Vescovo di Como'). Which image was crowned (the 'Ancona ... con l'effigie di Nostra Signora Santissima in piedi' over the privileged altar, or the facade statue with the Child) is not stated. OCR damage: many pages have marginal columns of broken word-fragments (pb 115, 117, 124-125, 129, 131, 133, 135, 137, 141, 143, 145, 147, 149, 151, 153).

sources.rubric_latin: BREVE quo Archiepiscopo Taurinensi committitur facultas solemniter coronandi, nomine et auctoritate Apostolica, Imaginem Mariae SS. Auxiliatricis.

sources.notes: Rubric OCR reads 'nomine et tauctoritate Apostolica' -> 'auctoritate'; addressee line OCR spaced as 'R i c h e l m y'. The Brief commits to the Archbishop of Turin the faculty to crown the image 'solemni ritu Nostro nomine et auctoritate', with a diadem to be imposed on both heads ('sacro utrique capiti tum Virginis tum Pueri Iesu diadema pro dignitate imponatur') - so the Infant Jesus is crowned as well. Richelmy to crown in the Pope's name (papal_legate_deputation is a defensible alternative). Exact coronation date not stated: only 'huius anni die per te eligendo', i.e. a day of 1903 to be chosen by the Archbishop. Datum 'die XIII Februarii MCMIII' = 1903, the second year of ASS vol. 35 (1902-03). Text of the act runs on to printed p. 581.

sources.rubric_latin: EPISTOLA SS.mi D. N. Leonis PP. XIII ad Moderatorem Generalem Salesianorum, occasione eorumdem conventus.

Same image as ASS 35, 580 (Maria Auxiliatrix, Turin); dedup expected. The letter itself names no church or town, but the address line reads 'Dilecto filio Michaeli Rua Moderatori Generali Sodalitatis Salesianae Augustae Taurinorum', hence Turin; locality/diocese/country inferred from that address line, so confidence lowered to medium. Datum OCR 'die x n Maii MGMIII' read as die XII Maii MCMIII = 1903-05-12 (Pontificatus anno vigesimo sexto confirms 1903). Coronation year 1903 inferred from the imminence of the congress relative to the letter's date.

sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child). Petitioner: PP. Chierici Regolari Teatini of the Giara, Verona ('porgere umile istanza all'istesso Reverendissimo Capitolo di S. Pietro'). Contents: (a) conto of the silversmith (f. 235r; signed 'Gio: Giardini Arg.ro' on the wrapper f. 238v) for two crowns 'all'Imperiale' of 15 December [1708] 'p.a La Madonna di Loreto e Bambino da PP. Teatini della Ghiara di Verona', 166 sc. 97½, final payment ordered 17 May 1709; (b) notarial act by Bernardo Ronchi, episcopal vice-chancellor, of the coronation performed in S. Nicolò by Bishop Barbarigo as delegate of the Chapter 'ex Epistola sub Dat. Romae die prima 8bris 1708', with chancery authentication (two copies, ff. 236r–237v; one copy's authentication reads 11 Aug. 1709, the other 11 9bris 1709); (c) printed 'Breve notizia' of the coronation, Verona 3 Nov. 1709 (ff. 239r, two OCR passes, text cut off at end of range). Coronation date: the OCR reads 'Die vero Dominica 19.a M[ensis] 8bris' 1709, but 19 Oct. 1709 was a Saturday, the stampa of 3 Nov. 1709 still calls the coronation 'da farsi', and the authentication is dated 11 Nov.; Sunday 10 Nov. 1709 fits all of these, so 1709-11-10 is a reconstruction (hence confidence medium; year 1709 is certain). Concession year 1708 inferred from the delegation letter of 1 Oct. 1708 and the margin note '30 9bris 1708 R. D. Barbarigo ad imponend. coronam deputatus' (f. 238v); no decree text is present. Crowns weighed 'Unciarum septem, unius quarti, et denariorum septem cum dimidio'. The Theatine provost was P. Pietro Paolo Masperoni. | Range opens mid-document: the closing formulae of the notarial act (notary Bernardo Ronchi, 'Veronae in Templo S. Nicolai Congregationis RR. PP. Teatinorum'), with episcopal authentication dated 11 Aug/11 Nov 1709 (OCR variants). Documents in range: notarial act close (237v inserts), Giardini's 'Conto 2 ... delle Corone d'Oro' cover with deputation note 30 Nov 1708 (238v), printed 'Breue notizia' (Verona, Fratelli Merli 1709; several copies, 239r-239v inserts), archivist label 'Relazione del origin. e promozione ... nella Chiesa de RR Teatini di Verona 1709' (239v.05), and printed programme 'Il Trionfo di Maria' fireworks for the coronation of the 'Madonna della Chiesa della Giara delli Chierici Regolari in Verona' dedicated to Bishop Barbarigo (240r-241v). The image is a statue of the Madonna of Loreto with Child made in Loreto and installed 25 Mar 1648. The programme says the bishop was deputed 'fin da principio' to avoid sending a Roman prelate; one garbled OCR copy (pb 567) mentions 'Monsignor Marchese Casali Canonico' as deputed, but this passage does not appear in the other copies and looks like OCR confabulation. Concession date not given in range (only the deputation date 30 Nov 1708).

sources.rubric_latin: Unicae Et Vetustissimae Viterbiensium Spei Ac Liberatrici Deiparae Mariae Virgini In Hac Vera Archetypi Sui Vultus Imagine Non Sine Prodigio Depictae
sources.notes: Crowns: two (Virgin and Child) — 'due Corone d'oro, una grande, et una piccola', made by Giovanni Giardini, argentiere, Rome, total 169.76½ scudi. Petitioner: Città / Magistrato di Viterbo (Comunità di Viterbo; letter of Bernardino Baroni, 25 May 1712). Letter of Bernardino Baroni (margin: 'Belardino Peroni', secretary of the Comunità di Viterbo), Viterbo 25 May 1712, about the city's failed plans to fund a solemn coronation and leaving it to the friars. Margin f. 123v labels it as concerning 'la Madonna S.ma della Quercia' - contradicting the letter's 'della Trinità' and f. 124r's 'Chiesa de Padri Agostiniani della Città di Viterbo'; probably an archivist's slip or OCR. Margin f. 123v: 'Decrevere 28 Maii 1696'. f. 124r: payment order of 27 Sept 1715 signed 'Moreno Vaiani Econ.o Dep.to'. No relazione or instrument in range and f. 124v is the last page, so the dossier likely continues. | The letter on f.122r (Bernardino Baroni, Viterbo 25 May 1712) opens mid-text with no salutation, so the dossier probably begins on the preceding leaf (outside this range). Concession date taken from the margin note 'Decrevere 28 Maii 1696' on f.123v; the same note reads the image as 'Madonna S.ma della Quercia' (OCR) whereas the letter itself and all other documents say 'della Trinità' / 'Liberatrice' — treat 'Quercia' as an OCR or archivist slip. The Latin instrument on f.128r reads 'die duodecima Mensis Iulii' (OCR), but the Breve Notizia, the pastoral letter, the inscriptions ('Idibus Novembris') and the archivist's note all give 12 November 1715. The pastoral letter (Card. Michelangelo Conti, bishop of Viterbo e Toscanella, Rome 1 Nov 1715, printed Viterbo 1715) and the Breve Notizia both survive in two copies (ff.127r, 130r–136r). Margin note on f.122r 'Sacra mad.na dal R.m... Ab.te d'Orvieto: Andrea Ricci al R.mo Cap.lo di S. Pietro' is obscure and may belong to another letter. f.136v.02 (pb 328) carries a stray list of Genoese-looking names (Martinengo, Giustiniani, Manganaro) with a marginal '181', unrelated to the coronation. The silversmith's account is dated 28 Sept / 9 Nov 1715; the first payment order is dated 27 Sept 1715 (Moreno Vaiani, Economo Deputato). | Only the last leaf of a dossier: a transcription of a votive inscription set up by S.P.Q.V. (Viterbo) on the Nones of May 1703 (Clement XI) thanking the Virgin for preserving the city from the earthquakes of that year; placed 'a parte Epistolae Maioris Altaris' (church not named). Copied 3 Oct 1856 by Alessandro D'Achille. f.140v-141r blank. No coronation data visible in this range; the dossier proper must precede f.140r.
Reported by Balzamo 2023, not read at first hand. Year only.

sources.rubric_latin: concedere La Corona alla Madonna S.ma delle Gratie in Malta esistente nello Chiesa Parochiale della Terra Zabar
sources.notes: Crowns: one requested ('concedere La Corona'). Petitioner: Francesco Pace, Maltese priest ('Fran.co Pace Sacerdote Maltese'), recommended by the Auditor Acquaviva ('raccommandato dall'Aud.re Acquaviva'). PETITION NOT CONCEDED — the image was not crowned. The Chapter's later docket on this dossier reads 'non si trova concessa' (Balzamo 2023, p. 189, citing BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, 4, f. 75r). Undated supplica; it cites as witnesses to the image's veneration the former Inquisitors and Apostolic Ministers of Malta: Cardinals Marescotti, Acquaviva, Ruffo, Pallavicino, and Mons. Passionei, Spinola, Caracciolo. ff. 75v-76r are blank; f. 76v is the docket ('Per Il Sacerdote Fran.co Pace Maltese p.r l'incoronatione di Una Madonna Miracolosa'). The range ends here, so any decree, instrument or relazione for Żabbar would lie beyond f. 76v and is not visible. | Petition only. Archivist's docket on f.76v: 'Per Il Sacerdote Fran.co Pace Maltese p.r l'incoronatione di Una Madonna Miracolosa — Non si trova concessa' (no concession found). Supplica cites Cardinals Marescotti, Acquaviva, Russo, Pallavicino and Mons. Passionei, Spinola, Caracciolo as former Inquisitors who venerated the image. 'other' = the archivist's docket note.

sources.act_type: Coronation reported by secondary literature, citing the Chapter dossier
sources.notes: Reported by Balzamo 2023, not read at first hand. NOT EXECUTED. sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. RODRIGUUM S. R. E. CARD. VILLENEUVE, ARCHIEPISCOPUM QUEBECENSEM, QUEM LEGATUM MITTIT AD CONVENTUM MARIALEM AD SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE VIRGINIS GUADALUPENSIS MEXICOPOLI CELEBRANDUM.
sources.incipit_latin: Mater spei et gratiae Deipara Virgo cum ubique terrarum sacraria, ubi perpeti benignitate filiis alumnisque suis cuiuslibet generis solamina largitur
sources.notes: Letter deputing Card. Villeneuve as Legate to the Marian Congress (NOT to a coronation); it attests the earlier coronation in passing: 'cum quinquagesimus feliciter plenus annus decurrat, ex quo B. Virginis Mariae effigies aureo serto redimita est'. Coronation year 1895 is computed from the fiftieth year running in 1945, not stated verbatim; day/month not given. Legate field left null because the deputation is for the congress, not the crowning. Passage printed_page 255; letter opens on p. 254.

sources.rubric_latin: CHRISTIFIDELIBUS DATUS DIE XII MENSIS OCTOBRIS A. MCMXLV, OB MARIALEM CONVENTUM AD SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE V. GUADALUPENSI MEXICOPOLI COADUNATIS
sources.incipit_latin: Venerables Hermanos y amados hijos que, reunidos en torno a la persona de Nuestro dignisimo Cardenal Legado, conmemorais los cincuenta anos de la coronacion canonica de la Virgen de Guadalupe
sources.notes: Radio message for the Marian congress marking the fiftieth anniversary of the canonical coronation of the Virgin of Guadalupe: 'conmemorais los cincuenta anos de la coronacion canonica de la Virgen de Guadalupe' and 'Hace hoy cincuenta anos ... cuando sobre aquella frente angelical resplandecio la aurea corona'. Coronation date derived from 'today fifty years ago' relative to the act date 12 October 1945. Body is in Spanish, so incipit_latin holds the Spanish opening verbatim (accents lost in OCR). The Cardinal Legate is not named in the text. The act begins on this page (264); the same act continues to p. 267, where a further papal act is recorded separately.

sources.rubric_latin: CHRISTIFIDELIBUS DATUS DIE XII MENSIS OCTOBRIS A. MCMXLV, OB MARIALEM CONVENTUM AD SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE V. GUADALUPENSI MEXICOPOLI COADUNATIS
sources.notes: Same act as AAS-37-1945-ocr#g264 (act begins on p. 264; this passage carries pp. 266-268). Pius XII, speaking in the first person to the congress gathered round his Cardinal Legate, says: 'Nos, a quien la admirable disposicion de la Divina Providencia confio ... el sagrado tesoro de la divina sabiduria en la tierra ... Nos colocamos hoy de nuevo sobre tus sienes la corona, que pone para siempre bajo tu poderoso patrocinio la pureza y la integridad de la santa fe en Mejico y en todo el continente americano'. This is a re-crowning (a new crown placed 'de nuevo') declared by the Pope by radio while an unnamed Cardinal Legate presided in person, not a first canonical coronation and not a coronation performed by the Pope's own hand; classified papal_personal_coronation because the Pope himself states he places the crown. The source never uses a word for 'image', naming only the devotional title.

sources.rubric_latin: Rosa Aurea Basilicae Beatae Mariae Virginis a Guadalupe, intra fines archidioecesis Mexicanae positae, tribuitur asservanda.
sources.incipit_latin: Flores edens et spargens, sive olim, uti ferunt, cum prodigialem praesentiam suam testatam voluit, sive continenter, cum caelestia munera ... supplicibus dilargitur
sources.notes: Golden Rose act; coronation attested in passing: 'Leonem Pp. XIII concessisse, ut venusta imago, qua Deipara, appellatione illa insignis, exprimitur, suo nomine et auctoritate aureo diademate redimiretur'. Year of the coronation not given here (see AAS 62 (1970) 681, 75th anniversary in 1970). Address form: 'Venerabili Fratri Michaeli Dario Miranda et Gómez, Archiepiscopo Mexicano'; the Golden Rose was to be delivered by Card. Carlo Confalonieri (bearer, not a coronation legate).

sources.rubric_latin: Universis Mexicanae Nationis christifidelibus, septuagesimo quinto exacto anno ex quo imago B. Mariae Virginis a Guadalupe aureo diademate redimita est.
sources.notes: Radio-television message of Paul VI for the 75th anniversary of the crowning of Our Lady of Guadalupe; the message body is in Spanish ('En el setenta y cinco aniversario de la Coronación de Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe...'), hence incipit_latin is null. Coronation year 1895 computed from the rubric ('septuagesimo quinto exacto anno') and the message date 12 October 1970 - not stated as such in the text; verify. The same event is listed in the volume indexes at pp. 876-877 and 911.

sources.rubric_latin: Mane diei 27 m. ianuarii, Polonorum civium coloniam in Mexico degentium coram admisit, antequam e Delegationis Apostolicae aedibus templum B. M. V. a Guadalupe peteret. ... Inde profectus, ad sacram aedem pervenit, sacris litaturus atque Plenario Coetui Episcoporum Latinorum Americanorum, intercedente Beatissima Dei Genetrice, initium daturus. Quae inter sacra, hanc homiliam habuit
sources.notes: Found by extending the search over the surrounding pages of the same journey, as instructed; this page is NOT one of the 26 passages of batch G07 (the id follows the batch id convention for AAS-71-1979-ocr, page 177). Homily/prayer of John Paul II at the shrine of Guadalupe, 27 January 1979, at the Mass opening the III General Conference of the Latin American Episcopate. Spanish sentence, verbatim: 'Finalmente, oh Madre, recordando y confirmando el gesto de mis Predecesores Benedicto XIV y Pío X, quienes Te proclamaron Patrona de México y de toda la América Latina, Te presento una diadema en nombre de todos tus hijos mexicanos y latinoamericanos, para que los conserves bajo tu protección, guardes su concordia en la fe y su fidelidad a Cristo, Tu Hijo.' Same pattern as the Altagracia passage: the Pope presents a diadem to a devotion named by title; no formal coronation rite is described, and the words are addressed to the Virgin, not to an image (the image is mentioned separately on p. 175: 'Tu imagen en el Santuario de Guadalupe'). The homily begins on printed page 171; the diadem sentence is on p. 177. Locality 'Mexico City' is inferred — AAS names only the 'Santuario de Guadalupe' / 'templum B. M. V. a Guadalupe' in Mexico (Tepeyac is named on p. 173) — hence medium confidence. Body is in Spanish, so no Latin incipit; rubric_latin is the Latin editorial narrative of p. 171 (ellipsis marks omitted text).

sources.rubric_latin: Memoriae proditur Summum Pontificem Ioannem Paulum II die decimo mensis Maii anno MCMXC in urbe Monterreyensi imaginem coronavisse Immaculatae Conceptionis Mariae, « Virgen Chiquita » appellatam.

sources.notes: The candidate passage is the volume's chronological index (printed page 1658), which points to the act at page 1512; per spec rule 5 the act's START page 1512 is used as aas_page. Full act text verified in txt/AAS-82-1990-ocr.txt at [[PDFPAGE 1512]]-1513: « ... aureo diademate, benedictione sacrato, sollemni redimiimus ritu ». sources.rubric_latin: Imago Beatae Mariae Virginis Immaculatae, quae sub titulo « Nuestra Señora de Monterrey » in ecclesia cathedrali Monterreyensi pie colitur, pretioso diademate redimitur.

sources.notes: Requested by Adolfo Antonio Card. Suárez Rivera, Archbishop of Monterrey (letters of 14 March 1996); the image is said to have been venerated there for 400 years. Country not stated in the act; inferred from the Latin diocese/place name.

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo Immaculata de Ocotlan
images.church_or_sanctuary: Ecclesia collegialis B. M. V. « de Ocotlan »

sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA VIRGO SUB TITULO DE «OCOTLAN» TOTIUS ARCHIDIOECESIS ANGELORUM, MEXICANA IN DITIONE, PATRONA COELESTIS CONFIRMATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Mexicana in ditione archidioecesis Angelorum intra fines exstat Sanctuarium Beatae Mariae Virginis de «Ocotlan» nuncupatae, quam christifideles regionis impense devoteque colunt.
sources.notes: Patron confirmation. Attestation: 'iam rec. mem. Decessorem Nostrum Pium Pp. X aureo diademate decrevisse Sacram Imaginem Beatae Mariae Immaculatae in sanctuario de Ocotlan servatae coronari' - so the coronation was decreed by Pius X (1903-1914); no date given. The act was issued on the occasion of the 4th centenary of the finding of the image, to be commemorated in 1941.

sources.rubric_latin: ECCLESIA COLLEGIALIS « NOSTRAE DOMINAE DE OCOTLAN » APUD TLAXCALLENSEM CIVITATEM, INTRA ANGELORUM ARCHIDIOECESIS FINES IN MEXICO, TITULO BASILICAE MINORIS ORNATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Quo Christifidelium pietatem impensius exacueret et amplificaret, Romanus Pontifex excultoribus Templis magisque religiosis ac frequentioribus decus addere solebat
sources.notes: Only an indirect mention: « Quinquagesimi vero anni a Canonicorum Collegio constituto nec non a peracta ipsius Marialis Imaginis coronatione faustam nactus occasionem ». The act is dated 22 Nov 1957, so the crowning fell c. 1907, but no year, authority or minister is stated in the text. aas_page = 558, where the act begins (the batch passage is paginated 559); confirmed by the volume index.

Simulacri caput tribus fuit redimitum coronis, quarum prima pluribus fulget adamantibus ». Year of the crowning not stated. aas_page = 302, where the act (rubric + incipit) begins; the batch passage is paginated 303. Text as printed says the collegiate title was obtained « anno MCCCCXXIII » from Pius XI — an obvious OCR/print error for 1923.

sources.notes: Basilica Minor elevation; attests 'Sanctus Pius PP. X, Decessor Noster, imm. me., concessit ut Simulacrum aurea corona redimiretur' - a coronation granted by St Pius X (1903-1914), with no year given, in the same act by which he named the Virgin, together with St Ignatius Loyola, principal Patron of the city. Country explicit ('urbi Mexicanae'). Act begins on printed page 1002.

sources.incipit_latin: Mirum in modum conspicitur, in loco eminens perexcelso atque edito, in parva urbe « Talpa » vulgo nuncupata, Tepicensis intra fines dioecesis, pulcherrimum Deo in honorem Beatissimae Virginis Mariae a Sacratissimo Rosario dicatum Sanctuarium
sources.notes: Basilica Minor elevation that attests the crowning in passing: 'Re vera ipsa Deiparae Virginis Imago, pretiosissima in Templo gemma, aureo fulgens diademate, quo sollemniter anno MCMXXIII per Capituli Vaticani decretum redimita est'. Country inferred from the diocese of Tepic and the intervention of Aloisius Maria Martinez, Archiepiscopus Mexicanus, both named in the act.

sources.rubric_latin: AD TITULUM AC DIGNITATEM BASILICAE MINORIS EVEHITUR TEMPLUM B. MARIAE V. A SACRATISSIMO ROSARIO IN URBE « TALPA », DIOECESIS TEPICENSIS, EXSTANS.

sources.rubric_latin: Sanctuarium Tlalnepantlanae archidioecesis, quod est dicatum beatae Mariae Virgini titulo « Nuestra Señora de los Remedios » invocatae, ad Basilicae minoris gradum dignitatemque evehitur.

sources.notes: Coronation mentioned in passing in a Basilica Minor elevation: the ancient image kept there was crowned in 1974 'nomine et auctoritate Summi Pontificis' as Queen of the diocesan clergy. sources.legate: Managuensis Ordinarius (Michael Obando Bravo, Archiepiscopus Managuensis, was the petitioner and is charged to impose the crown 'Nostro nomine et auctoritate')
sources.rubric_latin: Imago Beatae Mariae Virginis vulgo « Nuestra Señora de la Asunción » appellatae, in paroecia S. Mariae Magdalenae urbis « Monimbò » archidioecesis Managuensis exstans, pretioso sinitur diademate redimiri.
sources.incipit_latin: In paroecia S. Mariae Magdalenae urbis « Monimbò » intra fines Ecclesiae Managuensis praeclara exstat Beatae Mariae Virginis imago
sources.notes: Country not stated in the act; inferred from the archdiocese of Managua (Nicaragua). Monimbó is an indigenous quarter of Masaya, not named as such in the act. Coronation day left to the Ordinary's choice. Confirmed in the volume indices at pp. 1287 and 1312.

sources.rubric_latin: NUNTIUS RADIOPHONICUS A BEATISSIMO PATRE, DIE XXXI MENSIS OCTOBRIS ANNO MCMXXXXIII, IN FESTO D. N. IESU CHRISTI REGIS, CHRISTIFIDELIBUS DATUS, OB III CONVENTUM EUCHARISTICUM E TOTA PERUVIANA NATIONE IN URBE TRUXILLENSI COADUNATIS
sources.notes: Radio message of Pius XII closing the 3rd Peruvian National Eucharistic Congress at Trujillo. Spanish original, p. 356: 'para que Tu, Virgen de la Puerta, solemnemente coronada el pasado miercoles'; Italian version, p. 359 (this passage): 'Tu, Vergine della Puerta, incoronata solennemente lo scorso mercoledi'. The source names only the devotional title, never an image, and does not state under whose authority the crowning took place; it is the Pope himself who acknowledges it, and the Congress was presided by his Legate. The act begins on p. 353 (Spanish) with the Italian version beginning p. 357; the rubric above is transcribed from p. 353, not from this passage. 'Last Wednesday' relative to the stated act date (31 October 1943, a Sunday) would be 27 October 1943, but the passage does not give a date, so only the year is recorded. Also greeted in the same sentence is 'Nuestra Senora del Socorro' of Huanchaco, of whom no crowning is said.

sources.incipit_latin: Ex historia ipsius Ecclesiae Arequipensis satis de venerationis cultu cognoscitur, quo complures quidem Peruviani fideles inde a saec. xviii simulacrum
sources.notes: Assigned passage is the Index rerum analyticus (printed p. 1219): 'B. M. V. sub titulo «La virgen de la Candelaria» in sacra aede oppidi «Chapi» intra fines archidioecesis Arequipensis pretioso diademate redimitur, nomine et auctoritate S. P., 465'. Record built on the act itself at printed p. 465, used as aas_page. John Paul II crowned it in person during his pastoral visit: 'libentissime die II huius ipsius mensis Februarii pretioso diademate redimire vi et auctoritate Nostra Apostolica voluimus'. Act is numbered III in the OCR although the following act is numbered VI — numbering may be defective.

sources.rubric_latin: ECCLESIA BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS DE MERCEDE, IN CIVITATE LIMANA, TITULO AC PRIVILEGIIS BASILICAE MINORIS AUGETUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Limana in civitate quoddam, Beatae Mariae Virgini sub titulo de Mercede dicatum, templum exstat, quod, uti traditur, anno MDXXXIV
sources.notes: Clause: « prodigiosa Beatae Mariae Virginis de Mercede colitur imago, quae die XXIV mensis septembris anno MDCCXXI pretioso diademate, sollemni ritu, redimita est ». No coronation date given (the first papal visit to Peru was in Feb 1985), hence coronation_date null.

sources.rubric_latin: De coronatione Imaginis B. M. V. « dei Carmen » quae in paroeciali templo oppiduli Paucartambo, in archidioecesi Cuschensi, colitur, a Summo Pontifice facta, intexitur historia.
sources.incipit_latin: Per litteras, die altero Septembris, superiore anno datas, Venerabilis Frater Alcides Mendoza Castro, Archiepiscopus Cuschensis, de bono gregis
sources.notes: Assigned passage is the Index rerum analyticus (printed p. 1219): 'B. M. V. «dei Carmen» in oppidulo Paucartambo in archidioecesi Cuschensi, a S. P. coronatur, 707'. Record built on the act at printed p. 707, used as aas_page. The crowning itself was performed by John Paul II at Cuzco, not at Paucartambo: 'die III Februarii, hoc anno, petita gessimus, quando Cuzci ... pretiosa corona redimiimus'. Requested by Archbishop Alcides Mendoza Castro.

sources.rubric_latin: CHRISTIFIDELIBUS INSULARUM PHILIPPINARUM OB CONVENTUM MARIALEM IN MANILENSI URBE COADUNATIS.
sources.incipit_latin: Venerables Hermanos y amados hijos que, en la ciudad de Manila, clausuráis el II Congreso Mariano Nacional de las Islas Filipinas
sources.notes: Papal radio message to the Philippine national Marian congress: « esa preciosa corona, que ceñiréis a sus sienes en el mismo día centenario de la Definición dogmática » — i.e. 8 Dec 1954, the centenary of Ineffabilis Deus. OCR reads « Nuestra Señora de Oaysasay »; best reading is Caysasay. The message does not state that the coronation was granted by papal authority, so evidence_type is a passing attestation only. Coronation clause on printed page 721; the radio message begins on printed page 718, cited here as aas_page. Date is from the footnote « Datus die 5 Decembris mensis a. 1954 ».

images.image_title_latin: statua Iesu Infantis
legates: Hildebrandus Antoniutti, S.R.E. Cardinalis, Praefectus Sacri Consilii Religiosis Ordinibus Sodalitatibusque praepositi

sources.legate: Hildebrandus Antoniutti, S.R.E. Cardinalis, Praefectus Sacri Consilii Religiosis Ordinibus Sodalitatibusque praepositi
sources.rubric_latin: Ad Em.mum P. D. Hildebrandum tit. S. Sebastiani ad Catacumbas S. R. E. Presb. Cardinalem Antoniutti, Sacri Consilii Religiosis Ordinibus Sodalitatibusque praepositi Praefectum, quem Legatum mittit, ut Caebuae celebritatibus praesideat, quarto saeculo volvente ex quo Evangelium in Insulis Philippinis primum est annuntiatum.
sources.incipit_latin: Aurora, praenuntia felicis successus, ante quattuor saecula Ecclesiae in Insulis Philippinis illuxit, cum Evangelium ibi primum est annuntiatum.
sources.notes: The letter lists among the fourth-centenary celebrations at Cebu 'Eucharisticus e tota Natione Conventus et coronatio statuae Iesu Infantis, in anteriore quadam expeditione eum in locum allatae', and deputes Card. Antoniutti as Legate 'ut Nostram veluti gerens personam, piis coetibus aliisque caerimoniis praesideas'. The text does NOT explicitly commission him to perform the coronation — he is sent to preside over the celebrations of which it forms part; a checker should verify. Coronation year 1965 taken from the celebration year (letter dated 25 March 1965); no date is given in the text. Sanctuary not named (the Augustinian church at Cebu is implied by 'sacram aedem, quasi matricem ceterarum'). Archbishop of Cebu named: Iulius Rosales. Vernacular title (Santo Niño) not in the text.

Sin, Archbishop of Manila, the task of imposing the crown in his name, in person or through another; no coronation date given. Petition dated 25 June 1986, supported by Ricardo Card. Vidal of Cebu. Country explicit ('in Insularum Philippinarum finibus').

sources.rubric_latin: Cestochoviae, occasione oblata coronationis quattuor Imaginum Beatae Mariae Virginis.
sources.notes: One of four images crowned personally by John Paul II at Jasna Góra, Częstochowa, on 19 June 1983 ('obrazie z sanktuarium w Stoczku, Diecezji Warmińskiej'). The Pope gives thanks to 'Matka Pokoju' (Mother of Peace) for over three hundred years of protection over Warmia, and recalls that Stoczek was the place of Cardinal Wyszyński's internment 1953-1954. Bishop Jan Obłąk of Warmia is greeted. Image detail on printed pages 938-939; act begins on p. 935.

sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. EMMANUELEM TIT. SANCTORUM MARCELLINI ET PETRI S. R. E. PRESB. CARDINALEM GONÇALVES CEREJEIRA, PATRIARCHAM LISBONENSEM, QUEM LEGATUM DELIGIT AD CONGRESSUM MARIALEM E TOTA LUSITANIA, AUGUSTAE BRACARUM AD SANCTUARIUM « MONTE DO SAMEIRO » CELEBRANDUM.
sources.incipit_latin: Iucundo admodum animo accepimus, proximo Iunio mense, Augustae Bracarum, in perillustri et prisca Lusitaniae septemtrionalis civitate, ad Sanctuarium celeberrimum « Monte do Sameiro »
sources.notes: Legate letter for the Portuguese national Marian Congress; the Legate (Card. Gonçalves Cerejeira) is deputed to preside at the Congress, NOT to crown, so this is a retrospective attestation only: 'praeclarumque Deiparae Immaculatae simulacrum ... Romae egregia arte confectum et a Pio Pp. IX ... sacro ritu lustratum, quinquaginta abhinc annos aurea corona ... est feliciter redimitum'. Coronation year 1904 is computed from 'quinquaginta abhinc annos' relative to the act date (1954); not stated verbatim. The statue was made in Rome and blessed by Pius IX. OCR of the rubric in the passage reads 'MONTE DO SAMURO' and 'CONCALVES CERKJEIRA'; corrected from the body text ('Monte do Sameiro') and standard spelling.

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo a Sacratissimo Rosario (Imago Deiparae a Fatima)
images.church_or_sanctuary: Ecclesia principalis B. Mariae V. a Sacratissimo Rosario (Basilica of Our Lady of the Rosary)

sources.rubric_latin: NUNTIUS RADIOPHONICUS A BEATISSIMO PATRE, DIE XIII MENSIS MAII A. MCMXLVI, LUSITANIAE CHRISTIFIDELIBUS DATUS, SOLLEMNIA CELEBRANTIBUS AD SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE V. A FATIMA, AUREA CORONA NOMINE SUMMI PONTIFICIS REDIMITAE.
sources.notes: Assigned passage is the volume index (printed p. 461); the document itself is the radio message at printed p. 264, used as aas_page. Body is Portuguese: 'por mäo do Nosso Cardeal Legado, acabamos de coroar a Imagem taumaturga' — the Pope crowned the image through an unnamed Cardinal Legate, so legate left null. Country explicit ('Lusitaniae christifidelibus'). Classified retrospective_attestation because the document is a homiletic radio message attesting the coronation just performed, not the deputation act itself.

sources.legate: Benedictus S. R. E. Cardinalis Aloisi Masella
sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. BENEDICTUM TIT. SANCTAE MARIAE IN VALLICELLA S. R. E. PRESBYTERUM CARDINALEM ALOISI MASELLA, QUEM LEGATUM MITTIT AD CORONAM APPONENDAM SIMULACRO B. MARIAE V. DE FATIMA.
sources.incipit_latin: Celeberrima sollemnia, quae abhinc annos quattuor flagrantissima animorum pietate in honorem Beatae Mariae Virginis de Fatima a Lusitaniae fidelibus peracta sunt
sources.notes: Reached from the back-of-volume index passage (p. 494: 'Coronatio: ... simulacri B. Mariae V. de Fatima, 267, 376'); the act itself is the Epistula on p. 376: 'perinsignem imaginem Nostrae Dominae de Fatima sollemni ritu coronandam censuimus ... Legatum Nostrum deligimus ac renuntiamus, ut in Sanctuario de Fatima inditam Beatae Mariae Imaginem nomine Nostro Nostraque auctoritate aureo diademate exornes'. The coronation itself is recorded in the papal radio message of 13 May 1946, AAS 38 (1946) pp. 264-267, rubric 'NUNTIUS RADIOPHONICUS ... SOLLEMNIA CELEBRANTIBUS AD SANCTUARIUM B. MARIAE V. A FATIMA, AUREA CORONA NOMINE SUMMI PONTIFICIS REDIMITAE' ('por mão do Nosso Cardeal Legado, acabamos de coroar a Imagem taumaturga'). Diocese (Leiria) not named in either text.

sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. FRIDERICUM, EPISCOPUM TUSCULANUM, S. R. E. CARDINALEM TEDESCHINI, PATRIARCHALIS BASILICAE VATICANAE ARCHIPRESBYTERUM, SACRI CONSILII PETRIANAE FABRICAE PRAEFECTUM EUNDEMQUE SUMMI PONTIFICIS DATARIUM, LEGATUM DELECTUM AD SACRA SOLLEMNIA IN LUSITANIA AD SIMULACRUM B. VIRGINIS MARIAE DE FATIMA CELEBRANDA.
sources.incipit_latin: Proximo Octobri mense, postquam Congressus Marialis ex omnibus nationibus Ulyssipone in Lusitania habitus fuerit, Anno Sacro, quem ad universum catholicum orbem extendimus
sources.notes: Letter deputing Card. Federico Tedeschini as Legate for the closing solemnities of the Holy Year at Fatima — NOT for a coronation; the crowning is mentioned retrospectively on printed p. 781: « quique eandem sollemni ritu quinque abhinc annos coronandam quoque decrevimus ». 'quinque abhinc annos' from the Datum (24 Sept 1951) gives 1946; the year is not stated outright. `legate` left null because Tedeschini was deputed for the solemnities, not to crown. Diocese not named in the act; Leiria supplied from the place name — verify. The candidate passage is keyed to printed p. 781; the act begins on p. 780, which is cited here.

sources.legate: Benedictus S. R. E. Cardinalis Aloisi Masella
sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. BENEDICTUM EPISCOPUM PRAENESTINUM S. R. E. CARDINALEM ALOISI MASELLA, PATRIARCHALIS BASILICAE LATERANENSIS ARCHIPRESBYTERUM, SACRAE CONGREGATIONIS DE DISCIPLINA SACRAMENTORUM PRO-PRAEFECTUM, QUINQUAGESIMUM SACERDOTII ANNUM IMPLETURUM.
sources.incipit_latin: Persuavi animi iucunditate accepimus, praenobilis sedis istius Praenestinae clerum fidelemque populum, egregio praeeunte Episcopo suffraganeo, concordi studere consilio
sources.notes: Jubilee letter to Card. Aloisi Masella; the coronation is mentioned only retrospectively on printed p. 467: « Peculiarem quoque benevolentiam Nos tibi significavimus, quum ad coronam simulacro Beatae Mariae Virginis de Fatima apponendam Legatum Nostrum renuntiavimus ». No date given for the crowning. The Datum on p. 468 is OCR-corrupt ('die xviii mensis Maii, anno MDCCCCIII'); the pontifical year ('quarto decimo') fixes it as 1952, so 1952-05-18 — verify. Country inferred from 'de Fatima'.

sources.rubric_latin: AD VENERABILES FRATRES PATRIARCHAS, ARCHIEPISCOPOS, EPISCOPOS ALIOSQUE LOCORUM ORDINARIOS PACEM ET COMMUNIONEM CUM APOSTOLICA SEDE HABENTES: DE REGALI BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS DIGNITATE EIUSQUE FESTO INSTITUENDO.
sources.incipit_latin: Ad Caeli Reginam, inde a primis Catholicae Ecclesiae saeculis, supplices preces ac laudis pietatisque cantus christianus populus adhibuit
sources.notes: Encyclical 'Ad caeli Reginam'. The act opens on printed p. 625; the coronation clause falls on p. 627, so aas_page is the act's start page (which here also equals the passage's printed_page). Clause: '...radiophonicum nuntium, quem ad Lusitanorum populum transmisimus, cum prodigialis Mariae Virginis imago, quae Fatimae colitur, aureo diademate redimita fuit' (OCR renders 'colitur' as 'eolito'). Footnote 3 cites A.A.S. 38 (1946) p. 264 — the radio message accompanying the 1946 crowning at Fátima — but this passage states no date, so coronation_date is null. Country inferred from 'ad Lusitanorum populum' + 'Fatimae'; no diocese or sanctuary named.

sources.rubric_latin: ECCLESIA PRINCIPALIS B. MARIAE V. A SACRATISSIMO ROSARIO, IN LOCO FATIMA LEIRIENSIS DIOECESIS POSITA, BASILICAE MINORIS TITULO HONORIBUSQUE DECORATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Luce superna caliginosum saeculum illustranti, Beatae Mariae Virgini sacra est augusta Aedes Fatimae, in Lusitanorum finibus, ubi eadem Deipara, e Rosarii nomine nuncupata, olim se dedit conspiciendam.
sources.notes: Basilica Minor elevation act; states in passing 'sive cum Imago Deiparae aureo diademate, Nostro nomine et auctoritate, anno scilicet MCMXLVI, redimiretur' - crowned 1946 in the Pope's name and by his authority; the crowning Legate is not named in the act. Country explicit ('in Lusitanorum finibus'). The act rubric and body begin on printed page 210.

sources.rubric_latin: Ad universos Episcopos pacem et communionem cum Apostolica Sede habentes: de Beata Virgine Maria, Matre Ecclesiae omniumque virtutum exemplari, veneranda atque imitanda.
sources.incipit_latin: SIGNUM MAGNUM, quod sanctus Ioannes Apostolus in caelo suspexit, Mulierem videlicet amictam sole, non immerito de beatissima Maria Virgine ... interpretatur
sources.notes: Not an act about a coronation: the attestation is in footnote 6 of the Apostolic Exhortation Signum magnum - 'Nuntius Radiophonicus a Pio XII, die 13 mensis Maii anno 1946, Lusitaniae christifidelibus datus, sollemnia celebrantibus ad templum B. Mariae Fatimensis, aurea corona nomine Summi Pontificis redimitae: A. A. S. 38 (1946) p. 264'. Coronation date taken as the day of those solemnities (13 May 1946) - verify. The exhortation begins on p. 465 (rubric and incipit taken from there); the footnote is on p. 466. Locality 'Fátima' inferred from 'Fatimensis'; country explicit (Lusitania).

sources.incipit_latin: Quam pulchra, immortalis, frugifera ac triumphis assuefacta Fides, a Christo Domino nobis indita, sit, per varie tentatos ac vexatos populos clare comprobatur.
sources.notes: Basilica Minor act. Coronation grant attested: 'Anno praesertim MDCCCLXIV, trecentesimo ab ipsa condita ecclesia, Servus Dei Pius Pp. IX, Decessor Noster, praeter nonnullas Indulgentias, Marialis simulacri coronationem concessit et largitus est' — Pius IX granted the coronation in 1864 (the year the grant was made; the ceremony's date is not given). OCR forms: 'MDCCCLX i v' = MDCCCLXIV; place 'Sassinii'/'Sassinio', vulgo 'Sastinkse Straze' = Šaštínske Stráže (Šaštín-Stráže). Incipit OCR 'triumphis assuefa Fides' repaired to 'assuefacta'.
