images.church_or_sanctuary: Ecclesia Beatae Mariae Virginis Gratiarum in Monte Sancto
images.locality: Mons Sanctus prope Urbem Goritiam (Monte Santo / Sveta Gora, near Gorizia)

sources.rubric_latin: Ecclesia B. Mariae Virginis Gratiarum in Monte Sancto ad dignitatem Basilicae minoris evehitur.
sources.incipit_latin: In sublimi Beati Petri Cathedra, ad quam licet immerentes evecti sumus, nihil potius habemus, quam sacrarum aedium honor et cultus magis magisque in dies augeatur.
sources.notes: Brief elevating the church to a minor basilica; the coronation is mentioned in passing: 'venerata Deiparae Virginis Imago quae summa religione ibidem colitur iam inde ab anno MDCCXVII ex decreto Capituli Vaticani aureo diademate ornata sit' — i.e. crowned with a golden diadem in 1717 by decree of the Vatican Chapter. The act begins on printed p. 19 (rubric + 'AD PERPETUAM REI MEMORIAM'); the coronation sentence itself falls on p. 20, which is the passage's printed_page. Datum line reads 'die XIX Novembris MCMVI, Pontificatus Nostri anno quarto' = 1906-11-19, one year earlier than the volume year (ASS 40 = 1907); trusted the act. The text places the shrine 'prope Urbem Goritiensem' in 'Austriacae Ditionis' (Austrian Littoral, county of Gorizia, 1907); the modern country is inferred — Sveta Gora / Monte Santo lies today in Slovenia, above Nova Gorica, just across the Italian border — hence confidence lowered to medium. Raw OCR: 'celebérrimas' for 'celeberrimas'. No vernacular title given in the text.

images.image_title_vernacular: Nuestra Señora de la Peña de Francia
images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo « Peña de Francia »
images.church_or_sanctuary: sacra aedes seu sanctuarium Beatae Mariae Virginis « Peña de Francia » (entrusted to the Order of Preachers)

sources.rubric_latin: Beata Maria Virgo « Peña de Francia » vulgo appellata, principalis caelestis Patrona civilis provinciae Salmantinae eligitur.
sources.incipit_latin: Singulari pietate excoli perhibetur Beata Maria Virgo, cuius, adiecto vulgari nomine « Peña de Francia » appellatae, sedes praecipua finibus dioecesis Salmantinae continetur.
sources.notes: Patronage act; coronation attested in passing: 'Effigies denique, Pio Pp. XII Catholicam Ecclesiam regente, aureo diademate fuit, anno MCMLII, sollemniter redimita'. aas_page set to 794 (the rubric stands before the running head '795' in the passage; the passage was indexed as printed_page 795). No town named - only that the shrine lies within the diocese of Salamanca. Country explicit (Hispania).

images.church_or_sanctuary: Ecclesia concathedralis S. Nicolai, Alicante

sources.rubric_latin: Imago Beatae Mariae Virginis sub titulo « Nuestra Señora del Remedio », quae in Lucentina ecclesia concathedrali pie colitur, pretioso diademate redimitur.
sources.incipit_latin: Praeclarum confert donum christifidelibus diligens Deiparae cultus.
sources.notes: Granted to Bp Victorio Oliver Domingo of Orihuela-Alicante (letters of 23 Feb 1998). The volume index (p. 1055) prints the rubric verb as 'redimatur'. Country not stated in the act; inferred from the Latin diocese/place name.

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo de Aranzazu
images.church_or_sanctuary: Sanctuarium Beatae Mariae Virginis de Aranzazu (Franciscan friars)

sources.rubric_latin: SANCTUARIUM B. M. V. DE ARANZAZU, DIOECESIS VICTORIENSIS, TITULO AC DIGNITATE BASILICAE MINORIS COHONESTATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: In Cantabris montibus, dioecesis Victoriensis intra fines, haud procul ab « Onate », quod est provinciae Guipuzcoae oppidum
sources.notes: Basilica Minor act stating 'eandemque anno MDCCCLXXXVI, clero populoque plaudente, a Victoriensi Episcopo aureo diademate redimitam' - crowned in 1886 by the Bishop of Vitoria; papal authority for that crowning is NOT stated in the passage, hence confidence medium. The same act recalls that Benedict XV himself declared the Virgin of Aranzazu principal patroness of the civil province of Guipuzcoa in 1918. Old stone image of the Virgin with the Infant Jesus. OCR gives 'Ofiate'/'Onate' for Onate (Onati).

images.image_title_vernacular: Mare de Déu de la Mercè / Nuestra Señora de la Merced
images.image_title_latin: pervetus Virginis Mercedoniae simulacrum, catalaunica arte ex ligno mirifice sculptum
images.church_or_sanctuary: Regale templum parochiale B. Mariae Virginis de Mercede

sources.rubric_latin: TEMPLUM B. MARIAE VIRG. DE MERCEDE IN CIVITATE BARCINONENSI TITULO ET PRIVILEGIIS BASILICAE MINORIS DECORATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Conspicua templa in memoriam magni alicuius eventus erecta, quaeque non minus artis operibus quam et cultus splendore et potissimum fidelium pietate praestent
sources.notes: 'dum Leo XIII tam insigne simulacrum aurea corona redimiendum sollemniter decrevit' - no year is given, so coronation_date is null; it falls within the pontificate of Leo XIII (1878-1903). The act begins on printed p. 435 (passage printed_page is 436).

images.image_title_vernacular: Nuestra Señora de la Misericordia (Mare de Déu de la Misericòrdia), Burriana

sources.rubric_latin: Beatae Mariae Virginis sub vocabulo « Nuestra Señora de la Misericordia » imago, quae in urbe Burriana colitur, nomine et auctoritate Summi Pontificis coronatur.
sources.incipit_latin: Procedentibus christianae salutis temporibus omnium ordinum fideles ad Virginem Mariam fidenti animo decurrerunt, probe scientes superna se beneficia indulgenter accepturos.
sources.notes: Requested by Bp Juan Antonio Reig Pla of Segorbe-Castellón. The church/sanctuary is not named in the act. OCR of the incipit reads 'Procendentibus'; the volume index (p. 1057) has 'Procedentibus'. Country not stated in the act; inferred from the Latin diocese/place name.

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria semper Virgo a Misericordia
images.church_or_sanctuary: Sanctuarium B. Mariae semper Virginis a Misericordia / ecclesia paroecialis loci « Canet de Mar »

sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA V. SUB NOMINE « NUESTRA SEÑORA DE LA MISERICORDIA » IN ECCLESIA PAROECIALI LOCI « CANET DE MAR » VENERATA, PATRONA CAELESTIS DECLARATUR UNIVERSAE REGIONIS, QUAE « COMARCA DEL MARESMA » APPELLATUR, INTRA FINES GERUNDENSIS DIOECESIS.
sources.incipit_latin: Quae a Christianis « Mater Misericordiae » fidenti animo est appellata, numquam eorum fefellit spem, sed potius materni Cordis sui thesauros quam maxime ostendit.
sources.notes: Patron-declaration act; attests 'aureo diademate, quod, sacrae Imagini anno MCMVII impositum, illius honori, eodem peracto bello, est reiectum' (crown imposed 1907, restored after the civil war), and mentions the 'quinquagesimi a peracta Marialis Iconis coronatione anniversarii' - the 1957 act marks the 50th anniversary of the coronation. Authority of the 1907 coronation is not stated in the act. Rubric OCR 'LICI' repaired to 'LOCI'; OCR 'Marialis leonis' read as 'Marialis Iconis'. Country explicit ('in Hispania').

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo titulo « Nuestra Señora de la Fuensanta »

sources.rubric_latin: Imago Beatae Mariae Virginis titulo « Nuestra Señora de la Fuensanta » invocatae, quae pie colitur in Hispaniae urbe Cordium, pretioso diademate redimiri sinitur « nomine et auctoritate Summi Pontificis ».
sources.incipit_latin: Cordubae, in antiqua et insigni Hispaniae urbe, iam a saeculo xv a fidelibus loci totiusque dioecesis peculiari veneratione colitur decora imago
sources.notes: Rubric as printed reads « in Hispaniae urbe Cordium »; the volume index and the body of the act read Corduba/Cordubae. Petition of Bishop José Antonio Infantes Florido, letters of 23 July 1993. Coronation to be performed in the Pope's name; no shrine church named in the passage.

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo de Uribarri
images.church_or_sanctuary: Templum archipresbyterale de Durango

sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA VIRGO, SUB TITULO « DE URIBARRI », QUAE IN OPPIDO « DURANGO » VICTORIENSIS DIOECESIS VENERATUR, TOTIUS ARCHIPRESBYTERALIS REGIONIS DURANGUENSIS PATRONA COELESTIS DECLARATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Victoriensis dioecesis intra fines, in oppidi « Durango » nuncupati templo archipresbyterali, Imago quaedam Beatae Mariae Virginis religiosissime colitur sub populari titulo « de Uribarri »
sources.notes: Patron declaration that also grants the coronation: 'ut Imaginem eandem corona Nomine Nostro redimiri decerneremus ... ipsi Venerabili Fratri Episcopo titulo Siandensi, Victoriensis dioecesis Apostolico Administratori, eas partes committimus ut Imaginem ... aureo diademate, nomine atque auctoritate Nostris, sollemniter redimiat'. The executor is the titular Bishop of 'Siandensis', Apostolic Administrator of Vitoria; his personal name is not given in the act, so legate left null. Date of coronation left to him ('die ab eodem statuendo'). Passage printed_page was 221; act begins on printed p. 220. Vernacular title supplied as the Spanish form of the Latin 'de Uribarri' (only the Latin form appears).

images.image_title_latin: Imago Beatae Mariae Virginis « Virgen de los desamparados »
images.church_or_sanctuary: Sanctuary of El Saliente

sources.rubric_latin: B. M. V. imago populari sermone « Virgen de los desamparados » appellata, quae in Sanctuario loci v. d. « El Saliente » asservatur, sacro diademate redimitur.
sources.incipit_latin: Ministerii Nostri pontificalis ab initio Virginis Mariae cultum apud Dei plebem excitandum atque adeo augendum curavimus
sources.notes: Act begins on printed page 366 (passage printed_page is 365). Faculty granted to Emmanuel O. Hervás, Bishop of Almería (petition dated 8 Oct.), or a delegate, to crown the image in the Pope's name; no coronation date given. Country not named in the act: inferred from the diocese of Almería. OCR reads 'EI Saliente' for 'El Saliente'.

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo de Guadalupe
images.church_or_sanctuary: Templum B. Mariae Virginis de Guadalupe (Monasterium)

sources.rubric_latin: ECCLESIA B. MARIAE V. «DE GUADALUPE», INTRA FINES TOLETANAE ARCHIDIOECESIS EXSTANS, TITULO BASILICAE MINORIS EXORNATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Augusta Virgo Deipara, quam « de Guadalupe » vulgo appellant, religiosissima est, ut omnes norunt, apud Hispaniae gentes
sources.notes: Basilica Minor act stating in passing that the Apostolic See 'anno MDCCCCXXVIII eius Imaginem aureo diademate, augusto Ecclesiae ritu, siverit redimiri'. The coronation clause falls on printed p. 492; the act opens on printed p. 491, which is used as aas_page. This is the Spanish Guadalupe in Extremadura (archdiocese of Toledo), not the Mexican one.

sources.rubric_latin: Simulacrum Beatae Mariae Virginis, quae in dioecesi Onubensi pie sub titulo « Nuestra Señora de la Cinta » excolitur, merito diademate redimitur.
sources.incipit_latin: Satis compertum habetur Christifideles Onubenses iam dudum certo venerationis cultu Beatam Mariam Virginem, vulgo « Nuestra Señora de la Cinta » appellatam, prosequi consuevisse
sources.notes: Country Spain inferred from the see of Huelva (Onubensis); not named in the act. The act recalls that Paul VI declared her Patroness of the city of Huelva by the Letters « Praeclara Dei Genetrix » of 30 June 1964. Bishop Rafael González Moralejo is empowered to crown in the Pope's name. No church or sanctuary is named.

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo « de la Cabeza »
images.church_or_sanctuary: montanum sacrarium on the mount called « la Cabeza »

sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA V., « DE LA CABEZA » VULGO APPELLATA, PRAECIPUA APUD DEUM PATRONA UNA CUM S. EUPHRASIO, EP. ET CONF., UNIVERSAE DIOECESIS GIENNENSIS CONSTITUITUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Studium et cultus Beatae Mariae Virginis, quae « de la Cabeza » Hispanico appellatur sermone, a multo iam tempore animos tenent Illiturgitanorum
sources.notes: Patron declaration that recalls in passing that the Chapter of St Peter's ('Petrianae Basilicae Canonicorum Collegium'), at the request of Bishop Juan Manuel Laguarda Fenollera and in the time of St Pius X, granted 'ut ... Mariale simulacrum aurea corona redimiretur'; no coronation year given. The image, found in 1227 ('anno MCCXXVII') on the mountain, lost its diadem in the Spanish Civil War and a more precious crown was prepared to replace it. Act begins on printed page 383 (passage page-marker is 384). Datum reads 'die XXVII mensis Novembris, anno MDCCCCLVHII' — read as MDCCCCLVIIII = 1959, confirmed by 'Pontificatus Nostri secundo'. Locality Illiturgis = Andújar (identification supplied).

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo a nemore, seu « Nuestra Señora de El Soto »
images.church_or_sanctuary: Templum (cum coenobio) B. M. V. « Nuestra Señora de El Soto », Carmelitis Discalceatis creditum
legates: Iosephus Eguino Trecu, Episcopus Santanderiensis (Santanderiensis Ordinarius)

sources.legate: Iosephus Eguino Trecu, Episcopus Santanderiensis (Santanderiensis Ordinarius)
sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA VIRGO VULGO APPELLATA « NUESTRA SEÑORA DE EL SOTO » IN PRAECIPUAM PATRONAM REGIONIS « DE TORANZO » ELIGITUR ET EIUSDEM IMAGO CORONA REDIMITUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Potiora inter pietatis domicilia dioecesis Santanderiensis locum obtinet templum Beatae Mariae Virgini, Dominae Nostrae a nemore, sacrum
sources.notes: Coronation grant: « Santanderiensi Ordinario ... eas partes committimus, ut die suo arbitrio deligendo, post Missarum sollemnia, iuxta ritum formulamque praescriptam, imagini eiusdem Deiparae Virginis ... auream coronam, Nostro nomine et auctoritate imponat. » Date of the coronation itself left to the Ordinary, so not stated. Rubric prints the vernacular title twice inconsistently (« de El Soto » / « del El Soto »). Act date and page confirmed by the volume index (incipit « Potiora inter », 1959 Maii 23, p. 805 — same batch, AAS-51-1959-ocr#940).

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo de Monte Carmelo
images.church_or_sanctuary: ecclesia conventualis Carmelitarum Antiquae Observantiae (church of El Carmen)

sources.rubric_latin: Titulus ac privilegia Basilicae Minoris ecclesiae conventuali, B. Mariae Virgini de Monte Carmelo in urbe Xeretio dicatae, attribuuntur.
sources.incipit_latin: Actuosae pietatis domicilium sane licet appellari Carmelitarum Fratrum templum, quod in urbe Xeretio, intra Hispalensis archidioecesis fines, exsurgit
sources.notes: Basilica Minor act; coronation attested in passing: 'Marialis enim imago summae est omnibus venerationi, eademque anno MCMXXV, Patriarchalis Vaticani Canonicorum Collegii auctoritate, sollemni ritu coronata est'. Vernacular title 'Nuestra Señora del Carmen' is verbatim in the text. Locality: Latin 'urbs Xeretium', identified as Jerez de la Frontera (Carmelite friary in the archdiocese of Seville, Baetican province) — inference. Country inferred. The act opens on printed page 1119; the coronation clause falls on page 1120.

images.image_title_vernacular: Mare de Déu de Paret Delgada
images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo titulo « Mare de Déu de Paret-Delgada »
images.church_or_sanctuary: Sanctuarium « Mare de Déu de Paret-Delgada »

sources.rubric_latin: Imago beatae Mariae Virginis titulo « Mare de Déu de Paret-Delgada », quae pie colitur in Sanctuario eiusdem nominis in civitate « La Selva del Camp » intra fines Tarraconensis archidioecesis, pretioso diademate redimiri sinitur « nomine et auctoritate Summi Pontificis ».
sources.incipit_latin: Antiqua quidem et singulari pietate colitur imago beatae Mariae Virginis titulo « Mare de Déu de Paret-Delgada » invocatae
sources.notes: The act addresses « istis dilectis Hispaniae filiis ». Petition of Archbishop Ramón Torrella Cascante, letters of 9 Feb. 1996.

images.image_title_latin: Nostra Domina « de Indejo »
images.church_or_sanctuary: Ecclesia oppidi Las Fraguas

sources.rubric_latin: Imago Nostrae Dominae « de Indejo » quae in ecclesia oppidi v.d. Las Fraguas colitur, pretioso diademate redimitur.
sources.incipit_latin: « Dominus natus est ex Maria, humani generis in se peccata suscipiens, remissionem tribuit omnium delictorum » (S. Ambrosius, Expositio ev. sec. Lucam, VIII, 23).
sources.notes: Both the act and the volume index print the title as « de Indejo »; the shrine at Las Fraguas (Soria) is normally called Nuestra Señora de Inodejo, so the printed form is probably a misreading — verify. Bp Francisco Pérez González is deputed to impose the crown in the Pope's name (letters of 2 July 1996); the act mentions the 14th centenary of the diocese. Country not stated in the act; inferred from the Latin diocese/place name.

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo « de Lluch »
images.church_or_sanctuary: Sanctuarium (Collegium Sanctae Mariae) Beatae Mariae Virginis « de Lluch »

sources.rubric_latin: Titulus ac privilegia Basilicae Minoris Sanctuario B. Mariae Virg. « de Lluch », in Maioricensis dioecesis finibus, conferuntur.
sources.incipit_latin: Gloria et praesidium Balearum Insularum merito praedicatur Beata Maria Virgo « de Lluch », cuius venusta imago in Maioricensi templo, saeculo XIII eius honori exstructo, perpetuis impensisque obsequiis colitur.
sources.notes: Basilica Minor act; the coronation is mentioned in passing: 'Leo Pp. XIII, qui inditam imaginem illam per Legatum aureo diademate redimivit' (OCR 'redimi vit'; 'inditam' probably for 'inclitam'). No coronation year and no Legate name given; Leo XIII reigned 1878-1903. Locality 'Lluc' taken from the sanctuary's own epithet; country inferred from 'Balearum Insularum' / dioecesis Maioricensis, not stated in the act. Vernacular form of the title not given beyond « de Lluch ».

images.image_title_latin: Imago Deiparae quae vulgo a « Vallivana » appellatur
images.church_or_sanctuary: Ecclesia paroecialis B. M. V. in Caelum Assumptae, Morella (« Santa María la Mayor »)

sources.rubric_latin: PAROECIALIS ECCLESIA DEO IN HONOREM BEATAE MARIAE VIRGINIS IN CAELUM ASSUMPTAE CONSECRATA IN URBE « MORELLA », DERTOSENSIS DIOECESIS, BASILICAE MINORIS TITULO HONORIBUSQUE AUGETUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Pietatis monumentum singularis opusque factum arte eximia templum esse perhibetur Augustae Deiparae sideribus receptae sacrum, quo urbs « Morella », intra fines posita Dertosensis dioecesis, insignitur
sources.notes: Only: « Eodem in templo piissime excolitur, praesertim statis temporibus, imago miraculis illustris ac diademate redimita Deiparae, quae vulgo a 'Vallivana' appellatur. » The text says the image is crowned but does NOT state papal authority, date or minister — needs human verification before being counted as a papal coronation. Spain is explicit (« in publicis monumentis nationis Hispanicae »).

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo titulo « Nuestra Señora de los Milagros »
images.church_or_sanctuary: Monasterium franciscale « de la Rábida »

sources.rubric_latin: Memoriae proditur Summum Pontificem Ioannem Paulum Pp. II per Apostolicam visitationem in Hispania die XIV mensis Iunii anno MCMXCIII pretioso diademate coronavisse imaginem beatae Mariae Virginis titulo « Nuestra Señora de los Milagros », quae in franciscali monasterio « de la Rábida » nuncupato pie colitur.
sources.incipit_latin: Inter Apostolicam Nostram Visitationem in Hispania hoc anno die xiv huiusce mensis Iunii perquam libenter excipientes preces
sources.notes: John Paul II crowned the image himself during his apostolic visit to Spain; the act is the commemorative record. Petition of Bishop Rafael González Moralejo of Huelva, letters of 11 Jan. 1991.

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo « de la Encina »
images.church_or_sanctuary: Ecclesia paroecialis (Sanctuarium) B. M. V. « de la Encina »

sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA V., VULGO « DE LA ENCINA » APPELLATA, PRAECIPUA PATRONA CAELESTIS RENUNTIATUR OPPIDI « PONFERRADA » ET TOTIUS REGIONIS « EL BIERZO », IN ASTURICENSI DIOECESI.
sources.incipit_latin: Haud aliter ac multae in Hispania regiones, illa quoque « El Bierzo » vulgo nuncupata atque intra Asturicensis dioecesis fines posita, suum celebre religioneque frequens Mariale possidet Sanctuarium
sources.notes: « Anno insuper MCMVIII, quo Marialis ipsa Imago aurea fuit redimita corona, idem Patrocinium supra totam Bergidensem regionem ab omnibus vel publice est renuntiatum »; the act was occasioned by the 50th anniversary of that solemn rite. Rubric prints « PONPERRADA » (OCR/print error for Ponferrada). Crowning authority/minister not named.

images.image_title_latin: Beata Maria Virgo a Choro (sub titulo «del Coro»)
images.church_or_sanctuary: Ecclesia paroecialis matrix Sanctae Mariae

sources.rubric_latin: BEATA MARIA VIRGO SUB TITULO «DEL CORO», CORONA REDIMITA, CIVITATIS SANCTI SEBASTIANI IN DIOECESI HISPANIAE VICTORIENSI PATRONA DECLARATUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Urbis Sancti Sebastiani intra fines Victoriensis dioecesis in ecclesia paroeciali matrici Sanctae Mariae iam ab annis multis religiosissime asservatur imago Beatae Virginis Mariae vulgo «Virgen del Coro» nuncupata
sources.notes: Combined patron-declaration and coronation grant: the Bishop of Vitoria is charged to crown the image in the Pope's name on a day of his own choosing - 'Venerabili Fratri Victoriensium Episcopo eas partes committimus, ut arbitrio suo eligendo die ... Imaginem Beatae Virginis a Choro praedictam per se ipsum vel per ecclesiasticum virum in dignitate constitutum, et ab eodem deputandum, iuxta ritum formulamque praescripta aureo diademate, servatis servandis, Nostro nomine et auctoritate, post Missarum sollemnia, redimiat'. No legate is named (the ordinary or his delegate). Incipit ('Urbis Sancti Sebastiani') confirmed by the volume index on p. 583.

images.image_title_vernacular: Nuestra Señora de la Esperanza (Esperanza de Triana)
images.image_title_latin: effigies B. Mariae Virg., vulgo « de Nuestra Señora de la Esperanza Macarena »
images.church_or_sanctuary: Basílica de la Macarena (the temple recently built for her, per the text)
legates: Iosephus M. S. R. E. Cardinalis Bueno Monreal, olim Archiepiscopus Hispalensis

sources.rubric_latin: Ad E.mum P. D. Iosephum Mariam Sanctae Romanae Ecclesiae Presb. Cardinalem Bueno Monreal, Archiepiscopum Hispalensem, cum effigies B. Mariae Virg., vulgo « de Nuestra Señora de la Esperanza Macarena », ea in urbe aureo diademate fuit redimita.
sources.notes: Papal written message sent for the coronation day ('Hoy fiesta de María Reina ... se adorna con corona de oro y pedrería la imagen'); rubric confirms 'aureo diademate fuit redimita'. Act begins on printed page 598; the passage's printed_page is 599. Body in Spanish, no Latin incipit.

sources.legate: Iosephus M. S. R. E. Cardinalis Bueno Monreal, olim Archiepiscopus Hispalensis
sources.rubric_latin: Sinitur Imago B. M. V. vulgo « Nuestra Señora de la Esperanza » in aede S. Annae de Triana dioecesis Hispalensis, redimiri.
sources.incipit_latin: Qui semper castissimam Virginem Mariam, Christi Matrem amabilem, toto corde dileximus, aequo semper animo ea coepta aut inimus aut ineunda probamus
sources.notes: Act begins on printed p. 607 (running head in context); passage indexed at p. 606. Petition by Abp Carolus Amigo Vallejo of Seville that the crowning be performed, in the Pope's name and authority, by Card. Bueno Monreal, emeritus archbishop. Country inferred from 'in urbe Hispali' (Seville); not named in the act.

images.image_title_latin: Virgo a Sacrario
images.church_or_sanctuary: Cathedrale templum Toletanum (primatial cathedral of Toledo)

sources.rubric_latin: AD EM.UM P. D. HENRICUM TIT. S. PETRI IN MONTE AUREO S. R. E. PRESB. CARD. REIG Y CASANOVA, ARCHIEPISCOPUM TOLETANUM, DE CONGRESSU EUCHARISTICO EX TOTA HISPANIA.
sources.incipit_latin: Sacras inter aedes, quas catholicae Hispaniae filii, media aetate, excitarunt, principem videtur obtinere locum, cum ob molis amplitudinem
sources.notes: Act I begins on printed p. 52 (the passage page marker is 53). The Pope commends, but does not himself grant, the plan of the Archbishop of Toledo: 'itemque quam vos singulari cultu caelestem Patronam veneramini Virginem a Sacrario, eius effigiem aurea corona redimiendi. Utrumque autem, quod iam in eo es ut perficias, propositum ...'. Prospective, not retrospective, and not the coronation grant itself - classified as retrospective_attestation for want of a better category. No date is given for the crowning (letter dated 4 October 1926, coronation imminent).

images.image_title_vernacular: Nuestra Señora de los Desamparados / Mare de Déu dels Desamparats

sources.incipit_latin: Non levi animi delectatione nuper intelleximus de sollemnibus decies saecularibus, quae Einsidlenses monachi in honorem Deiparae « eremitarum Dominae » appellatae summo studio apparare contendunt

sources.rubric_latin: TEMPLUM DEO IN HONOREM B. MARIAE V. IMMACULATAE GENEVAE CONSECRATUM HONORIBUS BASILICAE MINORIS INSIGNITUR.
sources.incipit_latin: Nominis Catholici in urbe Geneva revigescentis signum perhibetur esse Templum, quod paulo post sollemniter pronunciatum dogma Immaculati Beatae Mariae Virginis Conceptus exstructum fuit
sources.notes: Clause: « Quod Simulacrum ... anno millesimo nongentesimo trigesimo septimo, Episcoporum, Sacerdotum e prioribus, populi fidelis astante corona, auro diademate, Nostro nomine et auctoritate, fuit redimitum ». The statue is the one Pius IX kept in his apartment and donated to this church. « Nostro nomine et auctoritate » is written by Pius XII of a 1937 event (reigning pope then Pius XI): read as ‘in the name and by the authority of this Apostolic See’.

Vernacular title not given in the passage.

sources.notes: Act declaring the image Patron of Uruguay; it attests the papal coronation grant in passing: 'utpote qui, facta anno superiore licentia idem simulacrum aurea corona redimiendi' — the faculty was given 'the previous year', i.e. 1961 relative to this 1962 act; no explicit date, so coronation_date left null. sources.rubric_latin: In Basilica Liberiana habita christifidelibus Urbis, in festo Immaculatae Conceptionis Beatae Mariae Virginis.
sources.notes: John XXIII recalls that Pius IX himself crowned this mosaic image ('il Pontefice Pio IX, con incomparabile solennità, incoronò l'8 dicembre 1869') at the opening of Vatican Council I, and that Pius X renewed the act with a richer crown on 8 December 1904, which the future John XXIII witnessed as a young priest. Act is an allocution delivered in the Liberian Basilica (St Mary Major) on 8 Dec 1960 but the crowned image described is the St Peter's Cappella del Coro mosaic. Act begins on printed page 30; attestation on p. 34. Body in Italian, no Latin incipit.

Country not named in the act: inferred from Caracas / archdiocese Caracensis. Datum 'anno MDCCCCLXXXVII' = 1987.

images.image_title_vernacular: Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe de El Carrizal

sources.rubric_latin: Imago Beatae Mariae Virginis titulo « Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe de El Carrizal » invocatae, Patronae caelestis Corensis dioecesis, pretioso diademate redimiri sinitur « nomine et auctoritate Summi Pontificis ».
sources.incipit_latin: Novimus clerum populumque Corensis dioecesis singulari colere pietate decoram imaginem Beatae Mariae Virginis titulo « Nuestra Señora de Guadalupe de El Carrizal » invocatae
sources.notes: The act records that she was made heavenly Patroness of the diocese of Coro in 1928. Bishop Roberto Ovidio Pérez Morales (OCR 'Raimundus Ovidius') is commissioned to crown the image on a day of his choosing, in the Pope's name; his petition is dated 13 May 1992. Venezuela named indirectly ('tam dilectis Venetiolanis filiis'). No church named.

images.image_title_latin: B. Maria Virgo de Coromoto
images.church_or_sanctuary: sanctuary of Our Lady of Coromoto, Guanare (the image 'será venerada en su nueva Basílica'); coronation performed on the explanada de Montalbán, Caracas
legates: Manuel Arteaga y Betancourt, Cardinal, Archbishop of San Cristóbal de La Habana

sources.legate: Manuel Arteaga y Betancourt, Cardinal, Archbishop of San Cristóbal de La Habana
sources.rubric_latin: AD EMUM P. D. EMMANUELEM TIT. SANCTI LAURENTII IN LUCINA S. R. E. PRESB. CARDINALEM ARTEAGA Y BETANCOURT, ARCHIEPISCOPUM SANCTI CHRISTOPHORI DE HABANA, QUEM LEGATUM RENUNTIAT AD IMAGINEM NOSTRAE DOMINAE DE COROMOTO CORONA EXORNANDAM.
sources.incipit_latin: Intra fines dioecesis Barquisimetensis, in Venezuelana Republica sitae, celebre admodum exstat Sanctuarium Beatae Mariae Virginis sub populari titulo « de Coromoto »
sources.notes: The batch passage itself is the volume's chronological index on printed p. 906, which points to the act on p. 722 ('quem Legatum renuntiat ad imaginem Nostrae Dominae de Coromoto corona exornandam 722'); the same act is indexed again at p. 942. aas_page is therefore the act's page (722), not the index page. Rubric, incipit, Datum and details taken from the act text at AAS 44 (1952) 722-723 in the full volume file. Act: '...perinsignem illam imaginem sollemni ritu proximo Septembri mense coronandam per Legatum Nostrum censuimus... ut in Sanctuario de Guanare venerandam imaginem Nostrae Dominae de Coromoto veluti manibus Nostris sacra exornes corona.' coronation_date = September 1952 ('proximo Septembri mense'); the volume also records a papal radio message of 12 Sept 1952 to the Venezuelans celebrating the coronation (p. 739). OCR of the act gives 'Guanare de los Oospes' (= Guanare de los Cospes) and 'Berquisimetensis' alongside 'Barquisimetensis'. Spanish form of the title taken from the radio message text at p. 739 ('Nuestra Señora de Coromoto').

sources.rubric_latin: NUNTIUS RADIOPHONICUS CHRISTIFIDELIBUS VENEZUELAE DATUS, SOLLEMNIA IN HONOREM B. MARIAE VIRGINIS DE COROMOTO CELEBRANTIBUS.
sources.incipit_latin: Venerables Hermanos y amados hijos, católicos venezolanos, que en la linda Guanare asistís conmovidos a la solemne coronación de vuestra Excelsa Patrona, Nuestra Señora de Coromoto
sources.notes: Radio message of Pius XII broadcast to Venezuela on the day of the coronation; the footnote reads 'Habita die 12 Septembris mensis a. 1952', which is the delivery date (there is no Datum line) and also the date of the ceremony. The text never uses a word for 'image': it speaks of the devotional title, the people 'colocándole en las sienes una preciosa corona' at 'la solemne coronación de vuestra Excelsa Patrona, Nuestra Señora de Coromoto'. It is not itself the granting act: the papal Legate was deputed by the Litterae at AAS 44 (1952) 722 ('AD IMAGINEM NOSTRAE DOMINAE DE COROMOTO CORONA EXORNANDAM', dated 30 July 1952, Card. Emmanuel Arteaga y Betancourt, Archbishop of Havana), hence retrospective_attestation. The message names the Legate only as 'Nuestro dignísimo Legado', so legate is left null; church_or_sanctuary, diocese_latin and diocese_modern are taken from that companion act at p. 722 (this passage says only 'el gran Santuario Nacional' at Guanare, Venezuela). Rubric OCR reads 'VENEZUELAS' for 'VENEZUELAE'. Incipit is the Spanish salutation, the act having no Latin body.

sources.rubric_latin: Memoriae proditur Summum Pontificem Ioannem Paulum II die septimo et vicesimo Ianuarii, hoc anno, coronasse imaginem B. V. M. de Coromoto, in dioecesi Guanarensi.
sources.incipit_latin: Sedi Nostrae beati Petri apostoli redditis, post peregrinationem in Americam Latinam, quanta subeunt, quae in tam longo itinere
sources.notes: Assigned passage is the Index rerum analyticus (printed p. 1219, which OCRs the diocese as 'Guaranensi'); record built on the act itself at printed p. 466, used as aas_page. 'beatissimam Virginem Mariam de Coromoto sollemnissima caerimonia coronavimus, pretioso diademate imposito ... die septimo et vicesimo mensis Ianuarii proxime elapsi'. Bishop of Guanare then Angelus Adolfus Polachini (Ángel Adolfo Polachini). Sanctuary not named in the act.

sources.rubric_latin: Caracae, ad Christifideles congregatos habita.
sources.notes: 'Hoy el Papa, Obispo de Roma, rodeado de sus hermanos los Obispos de Venezuela, va a llevar a cabo la coronación canónica de la imagen de Nuestra Señora de Coromoto, que será venerada en su nueva Basílica' (p. 832); the same act announces 'el acto solemne de coronación de la venerada imagen de Nuestra Señora de Coromoto, Patrona de todos los venezolanos' (p. 830, passage AAS-77-1985-ocr#v830). Act begins on printed page 828. Note this is a second coronation, the image having already been crowned at Guanare in 1952 (AAS 44, p. 739). Body in Spanish, no Latin incipit.

sources.notes: Basilica Minor elevation stating 'quae anno MCMX, auctoritate Sancti Pii PP. X, Decessoris Nostri, aureo diademate est redimita'. Act begins on printed page 885 (passage page-marker is 886). Vernacular title 'Nuestra Señora del Socorro' supplied as the standard rendering of 'de Succursu'.

sources.rubric_latin: Pii PP. X circa coronationem simulacri S. Cordis Iesu.
sources.incipit_latin: Me taedet preces tuas exaudire non posse eo quod S. Rituum Congregatio ultimis hisce diebus incongruum declaravit imaginibus divini Cordis Iesu coronas imponere
sources.notes: NEGATIVE norm, not a grant: Pius X tells Léon Gauthey, Bishop of Nevers, that he cannot grant his petition because the S. Congregation of Rites has just declared it 'incongruum' to impose crowns on images of the Sacred Heart of Jesus, permitting only that a crown be laid at the feet of the statue ('corona ad simulacri pedes deponatur'), which the bishop may do in the Pope's name. Emitted as `norms` per SPEC (general legislation about crowning images) with image fields null, though the letter arises from one concrete case: a simulacrum of the Sacred Heart in the diocese of Nevers (Nivernensis), France, for which no coronation was in fact permitted. Retained because it is the governing rule of the period on crowning Sacred Heart images and explains later refusals. Datum: 'Ex aedibus Vaticanis, die 9 Iulii 1908'. OCR: 'exaudiré' -> 'exaudire'. The letter is indexed at ASS 41, p. 621 ('Epistola Pii X circa coronationem simulacri S. Cordis Iesu ... 621').

sources.rubric_latin: NORMAE CIRCA PATRONOS CONSTITUENDOS ET IMAGINES B. M. VIRGINIS CORONANDAS — II. De Coronatione Imaginis Beatae Mariae Virginis
sources.incipit_latin: Pluries decursu temporis factum est ut populus christianus, filiali devotione permotus, ardenter peteret et obtineret coronationem alicuius Imaginis B. Mariae Virginis.
sources.notes: General legislation, not a specific image. Issued by the Sacra Congregatio pro Cultu Divino 'de mandato Summi Pontificis' (Paul VI reigning); signed Arturus Card. Tabera, Praefectus, and H. Bugnini, a Secretis. The document heading is on printed page 276; Part I (De Patronis constituendis) runs 276-279 and is dated 19 March 1973; Part II (De Coronatione Imaginis Beatae Mariae Virginis) runs 280-281 and is dated 25 March 1973 — that is the act_date given here. Key provisions: only images of the BVM (painted or sculpted) may be crowned; if Christ is shown with her, both must be crowned; the rite is normally performed by the local Bishop per the Pontificale Romanum; coronation 'nomine et auctoritate Summi Pontificis' by a Pontifical Delegate requires that the image be of real importance to the Church, nation or region, and 'facultas coronandi conceditur per Decretum praedictae Congregationis ac per Litteras Apostolicas in forma Brevis expediendas'. Passages AAS-65-1973-ocr#738 and #739 are back-of-volume index entries pointing to this same act at page 276 and were not emitted separately. Document spans pp. 276-280+.

images.image_title_vernacular: Beatissima Vergine detta di S. Luca

sources.citation: BAV, ACSP, Madonne coronate, tomo IV, ff. 74r–74v
sources.rubric_latin: l'istanza dai Soprastanti di cotesta venerata Immagine della Beatiss.ma Vergine detta di S. Luca, di fare alla med.ma il dono della Corona d'oro
sources.notes: Crowns: one ('il dono della Corona d'oro'). Petitioner: the 'Soprastanti di cotesta venerata Immagine' (via a request to the Chapter); the Chapter in turn asks an unnamed prelate ('V.S. Ill.ma') for a relazione. A single (draft) letter from the Chapter asking a prelate to report whether the image ('la tela predetta', a painting on canvas) is ancient and miraculous and has not already received a gold crown; no place, diocese, date or addressee is named. The 'S. Luca' title could suggest a well-known image (e.g. Bologna) but the text does not say so. A margin note at the head of f. 74r ('Instra Donationis Dna Coronat. amiea, fac' foras similiae miraculosi d.', i.e. 'Instrumentum Donationis duarum Coronarum aurearum factae simulacro miraculoso ...') is garbled; it may be the tail of the Cibona note on f. 73v or a heading belonging to this item — no instrument for the S. Luca image is actually present in the range. | Draft/copy of the Chapter's letter to an unnamed prelate asking for a relazione on antiquity and miracles of a painting ('la tela predetta') and whether it has already received a gold crown. No town, church or diocese is given; the famous Madonna di San Luca of Bologna is NOT named in the text and is not asserted here. A garbled margin endorsement at the top of f.74r ('Instra Donationis Dna Coronat. amiea, fac' foras similiae miraculosi d.' = Instrum. Donationis duarum Coronarum aurearum fact. simulacro miraculoso...) may belong to a preceding dossier not visible in this range; hence starts_before_range set true. No concession recorded in these pages.
